world: In the Realm, things that refuse to end don't. A warden keeps walking his rounds three centuries after the funeral. A choir keeps singing at the bottom of the bay. A fire keeps coming back. Adventurers call these places dungeons. The things inside them call them home, and every one of them has a reason it never stopped.

dungeons.name: The Sealed Crypt
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Gravekeepers in the Haunted Hills
dungeons.blurb: Low ceilings, damp slabs and coffins nobody remembers filling. The soul lanterns are the only light, and Mortis puts them out.

a.name: Soul Lantern
a.note: Light source · Goes dark in Lantern Out

b.name: Sealed Coffin
b.note: Blocks movement · Thralls climb out in Lantern Out

L.name: Warden's Tomb
L.note: Blocks shots · The grave Mortis rose from

lore: Nobody remembers who was buried in the Sealed Crypt, only that someone paid a great deal to make sure they stayed there. Mortis was hired to guard the doors. When the family stopped paying, he kept guarding. When he died, they buried him with his cleaver beside the others, and the next night he got up for his rounds.
The crypt has been opened from the outside many times. It has never been opened from the inside. The soul lanterns are lit by Mortis himself, and he puts them out when he wants to hunt.

dungeons.name: The Undersewers
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Sewer Rats and Plague Carriers in the Lowlands
dungeons.blurb: Brick tunnels, green sludge channels and the smell of ten thousand rats. Every grate leads further down.

a.name: Toxic Barrel
a.note: Blocks shots · Bursts into sludge when broken

b.name: Rat Nest
b.note: Spawns rats until destroyed

L.name: Throne of Grates
L.note: Blocks shots · Where he holds court

lore: The Undersewers were built to carry a city's waste away. The city is long gone. The sewers are not. The Gutterlord was a ratcatcher who went down one night to clear a nest and found that the rats had been waiting for someone to follow.
He wears a drain grate as a crown and sits on a throne of rusted gratings. His court is enormous, loyal, and very, very hungry. Every grate in the Lowlands leads down to him eventually.

dungeons.name: Mirewood Hollow
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Bog Witches and Marsh Lurkers in the Midlands
dungeons.blurb: A drowned wood of mud islands and bog water. Lanterns hang where there are no paths, and pink caps glow where something old is listening.

a.name: Seer's Lantern
a.note: Light source · She walks between them

b.name: Hexcap Toadstools
b.note: Decoration · Faint glow

c.name: Witch's Cauldron
c.note: Blocks shots · Bubbles over in Phase 3

L.name: Weeping Willow
L.note: Blocks movement · Something watches from the hollow

lore: Mother Mire was a village seer who could see a little way into tomorrow. She walked into the marsh because she thought she could see further from the middle of it. She was right. She never walked out.

Her lantern shows paths across the bog that only exist for a moment. Travellers who follow them arrive somewhere, eventually. The pink caps that glow in the Hollow grow where those travellers stopped.

dungeons.name: The Burned Forge-City
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Smelter Imps and Ash Golems in the Highlands
dungeons.blurb: Streets of charred cobbles cut by channels of running lava. The forges never cooled, and neither did their master.

a.name: Forge Brazier
a.note: Light source

b.name: Anvil
b.note: Blocks shots

L.name: Great Forge
L.note: Blocks shots · Cinder stokes it in Quench

lore: The forge-city made blades for every army in the Realm. When the fire came, the smiths ran. Cinder had one order left to fill, and he did not run. The city burned down around his anvil and he went on hammering.

Lava runs through the streets now, in channels that used to carry water to quench the steel. The Last Ember set was the order he was finishing. He will hand it over to whoever is strong enough to take it.

dungeons.name: The Moonlit Glade
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Dusk Moths and Pale Sprites in the Forest Edge
dungeons.blurb: A clearing that only exists at night. Silver paths wind between moonflowers, and every light is a lure.

a.name: Moonlamp Mushroom
a.note: Light source · Moths gather here

b.name: Silk Cocoon
b.note: Breakable · Hatches a moth if left alone

L.name: Moonstone
L.note: Blocks shots · Charges her Mesmer phase

lore: The Moonlit Glade is only there at night. By day it is an ordinary clearing; after dark, silver paths open between moonflowers that should not grow in that soil, and lamps glow where there are no lamps.
Every moth in the Realm is one of the Matriarch's children, and every one of them comes home in the end. She does not mind what else follows them in. She is always hungry for more light.

dungeons.name: The Unmelting
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Frost Wraiths and Ice Golems on the Snow Peaks
dungeons.blurb: The inside of a glacier: blue ice floors, snowdrifts and black water that never freezes all the way. Some of the statues used to be people.

a.name: Ice Crystals
a.note: Blocks shots · Shatters into icicles

b.name: Frozen Adventurer
b.note: Blocks shots · Should have brought a cloak

L.name: Frost Spire
L.note: Blocks shots · Rime's pillars grow from these

lore: The Unmelting was an ordinary glacier until a warm year began to shrink it. Something at its heart decided it would not melt, and it grew a will to make sure of it. That will is Rime.
It does not hate the people who come in. It simply notices that they are warm, and corrects the problem. Some of the statues in the deep ice were adventurers. Rime keeps them as a reminder.

dungeons.name: The Impact Crater
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Star Wisps and Crater Crawlers in the Godlands
dungeons.blurb: A bowl of scorched rock fused to glass where the star hit. Shards of it still glow, and the knight's broken shield lies where it fell.

a.name: Star Shard
a.note: Light source · Hums

b.name: Meteor Fragment
b.note: Blocks shots · Cover from the Supernova

c.name: Broken Shield
c.note: Decoration · All that's left of the knight

L.name: Fallen Star Core
L.note: Blocks shots · Source of the Starfall

lore: Astraeus fell for ten thousand years and landed on a knight who was riding home from a war. The impact fused the plain into glass. When the dust settled, the star had taken the knight's shape and the knight's sword, and was sitting in the crater wondering what it was supposed to do now.
Its siblings are still falling. On clear nights they land in the crater too, and Astraeus waits for them in the middle of it.

dungeons.name: Temple of the Twin Moons
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Sun Acolytes and Moon Acolytes in the Godlands
dungeons.blurb: Light marble and dark marble laid side by side, gold on one half and violet on the other. Every brazier has a twin.

a.name: Sun Brazier
a.note: Light source · Lumen's flame

b.name: Moon Brazier
b.note: Dark light · Noct's flame

L.name: Twin Moon Altar
L.note: Blocks shots · The moons cross above it in Totality

lore: Lumen and Noct were the twin moons' priests, a sister who kept the sun-fire and a brother who kept the dark. Twice a century the moons cross over the temple, and on those nights the twins become something more than priests.
The temple is split down the middle, gold on one side and violet on the other, and every brazier has a twin. The twins share one life between them. Hurt one and the other will make you pay for it.

dungeons.name: The Rift Beneath
dungeons.portal_from: Opened by the Unmaker's Eye, a rare event in the Godlands
dungeons.blurb: Islands of obsidian floating over open void. Magenta crystal grows where the Realm is thinnest, and something is always watching.

a.name: Void Crystal
a.note: Blocks shots · Pulses with the rift

b.name: Watcher
b.note: Invulnerable · Fires at anyone it sees

L.name: Shattered Monolith
L.note: Blocks shots · Its pieces drift apart in Singularity

lore: There is a place beneath the Realm where the Realm runs out. The Rift Beneath is the edge of it: obsidian islands floating over open void, and magenta crystal growing where the world is thinnest.
The Unmaker is not a creature. It is what happens to things that end, given an eye and a will. Everything else in the Realm refuses to stop. The Unmaker is where stopping goes.

dungeons.name: The Sunken Chapel
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Drowned Choristers and Coral Crabs on the Shoreline
dungeons.blurb: A chapel at the bottom of the bay. Water stands in the aisles, kelp grows through the pews and the candles still burn blue.

a.name: Drowned Candle
a.note: Light source · Burns underwater

b.name: Waterlogged Pew
b.note: Blocks movement

L.name: Sunken Bell
L.note: Blocks shots · Rings on every downbeat

lore: The Sunken Chapel slid into the bay during the evening hymn, and the Cantor did not let his choir stop singing as the water came in. It is still the evening hymn down there. It always will be.

Candles burn blue under the water. The tide comes in on the beat. The old lighthouse lamp the Cantor carries was taken from the shore the night the chapel fell, so that the choir could read their music.

dungeons.name: The Sworn Grove
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Grove Wardens and Sproutlings in the Forest
dungeons.blurb: An old forest held together by a promise. Paths of packed earth lead between braziers and stumps to the shrine where the oath was sworn.

a.name: Oath Brazier
a.note: Light source · Lit one by one in The Oath

b.name: Old Stump
b.note: Blocks movement

c.name: Shrine Stone
c.note: Decoration · The oath is carved here

L.name: Heart Oak
L.note: Blocks shots · One of Elderbark's saplings, grown

lore: Elderbark was the oldest oak in the forest when the wardens of the grove asked it to swear an oath: to keep the grove safe until they returned. They never came back. The oak kept its promise anyway.

The braziers in the grove were lit by those wardens. Elderbark only rests when all four are burning, as if they might still come home. Everyone else who walks in is, as far as the oak is concerned, a trespasser.

dungeons.name: The Stormcrown Peaks
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Gale Harpies and Thunder Hawks on the Mountaintops
dungeons.blurb: A summit above the clouds. Bare rock, old snow and a cloud bank that falls away to nothing. The lightning rods are not for your protection.

a.name: Lightning Rod
a.note: Light source · Draws strikes in Thunderhead

b.name: Storm Feather
b.note: Decoration · As long as a sword

L.name: Storm Egg
L.note: Blocks shots · Crackles when the Roc is low on health

lore: The Stormcrown Peaks are so high that the clouds are below you. The Tempest Roc nests on the summit and the weather goes where it goes. Shepherds in the valleys can tell when it is hunting by the lightning.
The lightning rods on the summit were put up by climbers who wanted to survive the storm. The Roc learned to use them. Nobody has ever climbed down with one of its eggs.

dungeons.name: Pyre Peak
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Ember Drakes and Cinder Imps in the Volcanic Wastes
dungeons.blurb: A volcano's summit of basalt and ash. Lava runs in rivers between the pyres, and the shells of old rebirths lie where they cooled.

a.name: Pyre Bowl
a.note: Light source

b.name: Phoenix Eggshell
b.note: Decoration · From its last rebirth

L.name: Phoenix Pyre
L.note: Blocks shots · Where Ignis is reborn

lore: Ignis has died nine hundred and ninety-seven times. Each time, it burns down to an egg on the pyre at the top of the volcano and hatches a little hotter than before.
Scholars say a phoenix has a thousand lives, which means it is nearly out. Ignis knows this. It has decided that if these are its last three lives, it will make them the brightest.

dungeons.name: The Burned Cathedral
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Ashen Acolytes and Penitent Wraiths in the Ruins
dungeons.blurb: The nave still stands, black with soot. A red carpet runs to the altar, the pews are burned to their frames and the stained glass survives in pieces.

a.name: Candle Stand
a.note: Light source

b.name: Burned Pew
b.note: Blocks movement

L.name: Charred Organ
L.note: Blocks shots · Plays the Requiem

lore: The Ashen Cardinal was halfway through the evening mass when the cathedral caught fire. The congregation fled. He kept going, because the mass was not finished.

The nave is black with soot and the pews are burned to their frames, but the organ still plays. The stained glass survives in pieces, and the light that falls through them still decides who the Cardinal will listen to.

dungeons.name: The Buried Oasis
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Dune Stalkers and Sand Scarabs in the Desert
dungeons.blurb: A drowned city under the dunes. Sandstone streets lead to a pool of turquoise water that never dries, and the ground hums.

a.name: Sandstone Brazier
a.note: Light source

b.name: Cracked Urn
b.note: Breakable · Sometimes full of scarabs

c.name: Wyrm Rib
c.note: Blocks movement · Older than the city

L.name: Sunken Obelisk
L.note: Blocks shots · Its glyphs light up when Sarrukh is near

lore: The oasis was the last water for a hundred miles, and a city grew around it. When the city dug its wells too deep, something under the dunes noticed. Sarrukh came up through the main well one night and swallowed the square. The sand closed over everything else by morning.

The city is still down there, sandstone pillars and all, around a pool of water that never dries. Sarrukh circles it endlessly, like a dog guarding a bone. Travellers who find the pool always say the same thing: the ground was humming.

dungeons.name: The Clocktower Court
dungeons.portal_from: Served by Bailiff Automatons and Clockwork Clerks in the Ruins
dungeons.blurb: A courtroom inside a clock. Dark wood, brass trim, and gears turning under the floor. The great clock above the bench decides how long anything takes.

a.name: Brass Lamp
a.note: Light source

b.name: Hourglass
b.note: Decoration · Runs backwards during Rewind

L.name: Grandfather Clock
L.note: Blocks shots · Strikes before every Time Stop

lore: The Clocktower Court was built to settle every dispute in the Realm, and the Brass Magistrate was built to run it. It has never adjourned. Four hundred years of cases sit in the archive, and every one ends with the same word: guilty.

The great clock above the bench sets the court's time, and the Magistrate can stop it whenever it likes. Inside the court a minute can last as long as the judge wants. Nobody knows who wound the clock in the first place, or what case the court is still waiting to hear.

dungeons.name: The Hall of Mirrors
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Glass Wraiths and Prism Sentinels in the Highlands
dungeons.blurb: A ballroom of polished floors and silvered walls. Every surface reflects every other one, and the reflections don't always keep up.

a.name: Glass Lantern
a.note: Light source · Its flame is reflected in every mirror

b.name: Shard Pile
b.note: Hazard flavor · Crunches when you walk past

c.name: Floor Prism
c.note: Blocks shots · Throws a rainbow on the floor

L.name: Standing Mirror
L.note: Blocks shots · Sometimes the reflection is a moment late

lore: Vitrea was a queen who could not stand to be unseen. She had her ballroom lined with mirrors so that every guest, wherever they stood, would be looking at her. Then she had herself made of glass, so that she would be in the mirrors too.
Somewhere along the way the reflections stopped needing her. They move a moment late now, or not at all, or do something she never did. Vitrea insists that she is the real one. So do the other seven.

dungeons.name: The Upturned Monastery
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Weightless Monks and Drifting Bells in the Mountains
dungeons.blurb: A mountain monastery hanging upside down in the sky. The floors were ceilings once, the bells hang the wrong way, and through the gaps in the flagstones you can see clouds below.

a.name: Prayer Lantern
a.note: Light source · Its flame leans whichever way is down

b.name: Floating Stone
b.note: Drifts slowly · Weightless

L.name: The Upturned Bell
L.note: Blocks shots · When it tolls, down changes direction

lore: The Monastery of the Still Peak was built for one purpose: to teach its monks to let go. Of wealth, of anger, of fear. Abbot Ossian was the best student it ever had. He let go of everything, and then, after sixty years of meditation, he let go of weight.

The mountain followed him. One morning the whole monastery tore loose from the peak and turned over in the sky, bells ringing, and it has hung there upside down ever since. The monks still sweep the floors, which are now ceilings. They say the abbot only wakes when someone climbs up to him, and that when he does, nothing in the room stays where it is.

dungeons.name: The Sundial Sanctum
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Hour Wardens and Sand Wisps in the Desert
dungeons.blurb: A sunlit temple built around a sundial the size of a courtyard. The shadows on the floor move when nothing else does.

a.name: Sun Brazier
a.note: Light source · Its flame stops moving during the Still Hour

b.name: Fallen Hourglass
b.note: Blocks movement · The sand is falling sideways

c.name: Broken Gnomon
c.note: Blocks shots · Its shadow always points at Aion

L.name: Great Sundial
L.note: Blocks shots · The Sun Disc fits in a socket below it

lore: Between one tick of the clock and the next there is a moment that doesn't belong to either. Aion lives there. Its sanctum was built around a sundial so that its priests could find the hour, and step into it, and pray for as long as they liked.

The priests are still inside, kneeling, perfectly still. Aion won't let anyone else in unless they can prove they understand the hour: break what must break, put back what must be put back, and do it all before the sand falls.

dungeons.name: The Celestial Atlas
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Star Cartographers and Comet Hounds in the Mountains
dungeons.blurb: Inside the Atlas there is no floor and no ceiling, only the night sky in every direction. Paths of starlight hold you up, and the edge of the page is the edge of the world.

a.name: Captive Star
a.note: Light source · A star Vael caught and never let go

b.name: Drifting Asteroid
b.note: Blocks movement · It turns slowly as it drifts

c.name: Ringed Moon
c.note: Light source · A tiny moon, close enough to touch

L.name: Star Lens
L.note: Blocks shots · Draws a constellation in its glass, one line at a time

lore: The Celestial Atlas is a map of the night sky, bound in a library at the top of the world. Open it to the right page and you don't read the stars any more, you walk among them. Vael was the greatest hunter of her age, and when she died the sky asked to keep her. She has been a constellation ever since.

Step inside and there is no library any more, no floor and no ceiling: only the night sky in every direction, held together by paths of starlight. Every star in it is a trail Vael is following, and anyone who opens the book becomes her quarry. Those who keep up with her say the strangest part is when even the paths fall away and you're simply flying.

dungeons.name: Duskmourne Keep
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Hollow Knights and Crownless Wraiths in the Highlands
dungeons.blurb: A dark castle on a dead hill. Red candles, empty armor in every alcove, and a throne room floored like a chessboard.

a.name: Black Brazier
a.note: Light source · Burns red and gives no warmth

b.name: Empty Armor
b.note: Blocks movement · Sometimes it turns its head

c.name: Faded Banner
c.note: Decoration · The crest has been scratched out

L.name: The Black Throne
L.note: Blocks shots · Its eyes follow whoever stands before it

lore: Duskmourne Keep was the seat of a good king once. Then Morvane took the throne and made a bargain with the crown: as long as he wore it, he would never die. The crown kept its word. It took everything else instead, one piece at a time, until there was nothing left inside the armor at all.

He still holds court in an empty throne room, moving his guards across the floor like chess pieces. The candles burn black. The banners have forgotten their colors. And the crown, which is all that's left of him, still wants a kingdom.

dungeons.name: The Hollow Patch
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Vine Creepers and Lantern Jacks in the Lowlands
dungeons.blurb: A pumpkin patch that never stops growing, lit by carved lanterns and fenced with vines. The pumpkins grin, and some of them follow you with their eyes.

a.name: Carved Lantern
a.note: Light source · Grins at you

b.name: Hay Bale
b.note: Blocks movement

c.name: Scarecrow
c.note: Blocks shots · Its head is a pumpkin. It wasn't last week

L.name: Prize Pumpkin
L.note: Blocks shots · Big enough to live in. Something does

lore: Every autumn the Hollow Patch grows a little wider and the Pumpkin Lord a little larger. This year his vines crept over the hills and into the orchards of the Melon Kingdom, and the Melon Queen sent her two best: Sir Rindley, the Kingdom's champion, and Sister Honeydew, its kindest healer.

They found the Patch and the Lord at the heart of it, and they found you, about to go in alone. Rindley insisted you come along. Honeydew insisted you eat something first. Neither would hear a word against it.

dungeons.name: The Velvet Stage
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Stagehand Shades and Phantom Ushers in the Old Quarter
dungeons.blurb: A grand theatre gone dark. Teal velvet curtains, a gilded proscenium, a single spotlight that moves on its own, and a magician's cabinet that nobody has ever seen open.

a.name: Footlight
a.note: Light source · A gas footlight at the lip of the stage. The audience can't see past it

b.name: Prop Trunk
b.note: Blocks movement · Full of masks. One of them is warm

c.name: Painted Flat
c.note: Blocks shots · A wooden tree, painted for a play nobody remembers

L.name: The Vanishing Cabinet
L.note: Blocks shots · The doors are a hand's width open. Something inside is breathing

lore: The Velvet Stage was the grandest theatre in the Realm, and its greatest act was Mirabeau the Magnificent. He sawed himself in half, escaped from chains underwater, and pulled more doves from his hat than the hat could hold. For his farewell show he promised the impossible: to vanish completely, forever.

He stepped into his cabinet. The doors closed. When the stagehands opened them, he was gone, and he has never come back. But the house lights still dim when you walk in, the curtain still rises, and the spotlight still finds you. Somewhere inside his own illusion, Mirabeau is still performing, and he needs a volunteer from the audience.

dungeons.name: The Paper Garden
dungeons.portal_from: Dropped by Ink Wraiths and Paper Cranes in the Scholars' Hills
dungeons.blurb: A moonlit garden folded entirely from paper: washi paths, fan-leaf trees, lanterns that never burn through, and a stream of black ink that reflects the moon.

a.name: Paper Lantern
a.note: Light source · A folded lantern. The flame inside is paper too, somehow

b.name: Paper Tree
b.note: Blocks movement · Every leaf is a folded fan

c.name: Folded Stone
c.note: Blocks shots · A boulder made of a single folded sheet

L.name: The Folded Pagoda
L.note: Blocks shots · Three roofs, each folded from a single sheet. Lanterns burn in every window

lore: They say that if you fold a thousand paper cranes, you're granted a wish. A lonely scholar folded nine hundred and ninety-nine in a garden of paper he made himself: paper trees, paper lanterns, a stream of his own ink. He died before the last one. So the thousandth crane folded itself.

Orrigan grants wishes the way paper cuts: quickly, and deeper than you'd think. The garden is its page now. It can fold the paths, spill the ink, and send its nine hundred and ninety-nine sisters across the sky in long white flocks.

bosses.name: Gravewarden Mortis
bosses.title: Keeper of the Sealed Crypt
bosses.intro: The last warden of a crypt nobody remembers sealing. He still walks his rounds with the cleaver he was buried with.

phases.name: The Rounds
phases.text: Mortis walks his rounds with his soul lantern held out. Its cone of light sweeps the crypt like a lighthouse beam, and anything it touches burns. He throws bones and cleaves at whatever he finds.
notes: The lantern turns at a steady pace: step out of its path, then follow behind it
The cone is only 9 tiles long, so distance is safety too

phases.name: Lantern Out
phases.text: He snuffs his lantern and the crypt goes black except a small circle around you. Four Spectral Thralls rise; he can't be hurt until they fall. Grave Wisps drift in, freeze, then lunge. Every shot glows through the dark, so you can always see what is coming.
notes: Wisps re-aim when they stop: sidestep the moment one freezes
Wisps stop your healing for 2s

phases.name: Unburial
phases.text: Unburial. The dead are restless and so is the floor: stand still for more than a moment and a grave hand bursts up beneath you. Rings of bones close in from the walls toward Mortis, and graves open where you stand.
notes: Keep drifting: a red ring tightens at your feet before a hand grabs
Closing rings leave gaps between bones: step through as they pass

phases.name: Funeral Bell
phases.text: Mortis sinks into his own grave and rises from another one across the crypt. Each time he surfaces the bell tolls: an expanding ring with a single gap. Coffin nails stop, re-aim and snap toward you.
notes: A green circle marks where he'll rise, and its open side shows where the gap in the toll will be
You get about 1.5s between the mark and the ring reaching you
He can't be hurt while he's underground: save your shots for when he surfaces

phases.name: Last Rites
phases.text: Rage. Last rites for the living. Mortis hurls bone bolas, pairs of bones joined by a spinning chain of soul-light, between rings of bone and cleaves.
notes: A bolas is wide: watch the chain, not just the bones
They spin as they fly, so the gap between them opens and closes

bosses.feel: A stalker in the dark. He walks you down and the floor itself is his weapon.
signature: Darkness with a thrall shield
Cross-shaped open graves
Sinks into one grave and rises from another
Bell tolls: rings with a single gap

cleave.name: Soul Cleave
cleave.how: Crescents peel outward in curving arcs

wisp.name: Grave Wisp
wisp.how: Hangs in the air, then lunges at you

nail.name: Coffin Nail
nail.how: Stops dead, re-aims, then fires twice as fast

bell.name: Funeral Toll
bell.how: An expanding ring of sound with one gap

thrall.name: Spectral Thrall
thrall.how: Shambles toward you throwing bones (3,000 HP)

bolas.name: Bone Bolas
bolas.how: Two bones on a chain of soul-light, spinning as they fly. The chain hurts as much as the bones

grasp.name: Grave Hand
grasp.how: Stand still too long and a hand bursts out of the floor beneath you

lines.t: Visiting hours ended three hundred years ago.
Mortis raises his lantern. Its light begins to sweep the crypt.
The lanterns burn for the dead. You are not dead. Yet.
Lights out. Count your steps.
Every grave in this crypt was dug by my hand.
Let me show you which one is yours.
Hear the bell? It tolls for whoever stops moving.
Enough rounds. I will carry you down myself!
Mortis knots bones together with soul-light.

death.after: The crypt falls silent. Somewhere, a lantern relights itself.

say: Mortis falls. The lantern rolls from his hand and goes out.

bosses.name: The Gutterlord
bosses.title: Rat King of the Undersewers
bosses.intro: He crowned himself with a drain grate and has ruled the sewers ever since. His court is ten thousand rats deep.

phases.name: Court of Rats
phases.text: He holds court from a throne of sludge. Rats pour out and rush the nearest player before bursting, and sludge globs arc out, stop, and splash into drops.
notes: Kill rats early or lead them away before they pop
The splash lands where the glob stops: don't stand at its full range

phases.name: Royal Tantrum
phases.text: The Rat King throws a tantrum. He rips a burst pipe off the wall and sprays filth across the room, sweeping it back and forth like a garden hose while his rats gnaw at everything.
notes: The stream sweeps one way, then the other: cross it as it turns back
It always swings around you, so keep moving sideways

phases.name: The Flood
phases.text: Sludge pours in from the edges and the dry floor shrinks every few seconds. Walls of bile roll down the room, each with one gap.
notes: Stay near the middle and read each wall early

phases.name: Gnawing Frenzy
phases.text: Rage. A gnawing frenzy: two spirals turn in opposite directions, gnashing teeth one way and bile the other. Every bite carries plague: while you're Sick you don't regenerate.
notes: The two spirals cross: find the diamond-shaped gaps where they pass each other
Avoid bites above all: being Sick stops your healing

bosses.feel: Chaos. Swarms, splashes and a king who throws tantrums.
signature: Rat swarms that burst into teeth
A boomerang crown that leaves him exposed
The rising flood and falling walls of bile
Frenzied charges

gnaw.name: Gnaw
gnaw.how: Scurries in a zigzag. Plague-ridden: a bite makes you Sick, and you won't regenerate for 3.5s

sludge.name: Sludge Glob
sludge.how: Lobbed; slows down and splashes into 7 drops

rat.name: Rat Swarm
rat.how: Rushes you and bursts into a ring of teeth after 3s

spew.name: Spew
spew.how: A stream of filth from a burst pipe, swept back and forth like a hose

lines.t: Kneel! Every rat in this court outranks you.
Who laughed? WHO LAUGHED?
The Rat King rips a burst pipe off the wall.
Open the gates! Let the gutters take them!
MY THRONE! MY SEWER! MY RATS!

death.after: His crown rolls into a drain. Somewhere below, a rat tries it on.

bosses.name: Mother Mire
bosses.title: The Bog Seer
bosses.intro: A seer who walked into the marsh to see further, and stayed. Her lantern shows paths that aren't there yet.

phases.name: Lantern Walk
phases.text: Mother Mire walks the bog and hangs a lantern wherever she stops. Lanterns flare when you come within 2 tiles, then burst into hexed petals. The paths she walks fill up with them.
notes: A flaring lantern gives you 0.7s: step back out of its burst
She leaves them where she's been, so don't follow her path

phases.name: Three Lanterns
phases.text: Two false lanterns light up and she swaps places with one every few seconds. The false ones bloom petal flowers; the real one sends marsh lights.
notes: The real Mire's lantern flickers; the false ones glow steady
The false lanterns can't be hurt; shots that hit them are wasted

phases.name: Bubbling Cauldron
phases.text: Mother Mire brews. Each time the cauldron boils, three runes light up on the floor: step on all of them before her brew completes and the ritual is spoiled, staggering her. Let it finish and the cauldron erupts, and the fumes leave you Confused, with your controls reversed.
notes: The runes are always spread out: plan a route through all three
Confused reverses your movement for 2.5s

ritual.say: The cauldron boils! Step on all three runes to spoil the brew.

phases.name: Lantern's Gaze
phases.text: She lifts the lantern and its beam slowly turns to follow you for two seconds. A two-armed petal spiral turns around her.
notes: The beam aims for 1s, then turns at 30° a second: circle her and it can never catch up

phases.name: Hexthorn Bloom
phases.text: Rage. The whole hollow is cursed. Dense petal flowers, homing lights and two sigils hunting you at once.
notes: You take 20% more damage from everything now: play safe
Her marsh hexes leave you Confused for a moment: controls reversed

bosses.feel: Trickery. False lanterns, curses that follow you, and a gaze that hunts.
signature: Hex petals that bloom into flowers
Swaps places with false lanterns
Curse sigils that follow you, then lock
A lantern beam that tracks you

petal.name: Hex Petal
petal.how: Curls in alternating directions, blooming into flowers

bubble.name: Bog Bubble
bubble.how: Swells as it drifts, then pops into 6 marsh lights

sigil.name: Curse Sigil
sigil.how: Follows under your feet for 0.8s, locks, then bursts 0.9s later

ray.name: Lantern Gaze
ray.how: A beam that slowly turns to follow you

lantern.name: Hanging Lantern
lantern.how: Left hanging wherever she walks. Get within 2 tiles and it flares, then bursts into petals 0.7s later

brew.name: Boiled Hex
brew.how: What spills out of the cauldron when her brew completes

lines.t: Lost, dear? Follow the light. They all do.
She hangs a lantern wherever she stops.
Which of us is real? Even I forget, some nights.
A pinch of hex, a stir of bog.
Hold still for the curse, there's a dear.
I see the path you'll take. It ends here.
The hollow remembers every footstep. Let it bloom!
There was never a path. There was only me.

say.t: Ah... so that is where this path led.

death.after: Her lantern gutters out. For a moment, every path in the marsh is visible at once.

bosses.name: Forgemaster Cinder
bosses.title: The Last Smith
bosses.intro: He was still hammering when the city burned around him. He hasn't stopped since.

phases.name: Stoking
phases.text: Cinder stokes the forge until the floor glows. The floor is laid in 3-tile plates, and every 2.6s half of them heat up in a checkerboard: they glow for 1.2s, then sear. The other half are safe, and next time it's the other way round.
notes: Stand on a dark plate when the glow peaks
The checkerboard flips every time, so you'll step one plate over each cycle

phases.name: Quench
phases.text: His armor overheats and he can't be hurt. Four bellows stand at the walls; all four must be held at once for 3s to vent the heat. Meanwhile four jets of fire turn around him like a wheel.
notes: Assign one player per bellows before the phase
Rotate with the flames, not against them

phases.name: Hammerfall
phases.text: He leaps. A circle marks the landing spot for 1.2s, then he crashes down in a shockwave that throws a ring of 14 sparks, and sparks spray from his anvil hand between leaps.
notes: He leaps at whoever dealt the most damage
He can't be hurt while he's in the air; hit him the moment he lands

phases.name: Molten Chains
phases.text: Molten chains whip out from the four anvils in the corners of the forge, a crossfire aimed at you from every side. Cinder throws slag that slows to a stop and hangs in the air, cooling, closing off the room piece by piece.
notes: Crossfire comes from all four corners: stand where the lines don't cross
Hanging slag still hurts. Thread between the pieces before they crumble

phases.name: Meltdown
phases.text: Rage. The forge melts down. The floor plates heat up faster while sparks spiral out of the boss and molten rings follow.
notes: Pick your dark plate first, then dodge

bosses.feel: Heavy and deliberate. Every hit lands like a hammer.
signature: Anvil sprays
Four bellows that must be held together
Leaps across the forge and slams
Pinwheeling molten chains

slag.name: Slag
slag.how: Slows to a stop, then bursts into sparks

flame.name: Bellows Flame
flame.how: Short jet of fire that billows outward

chain.name: Molten Chain
chain.how: Links that pinwheel around their path

hammer.name: Hammerfall
hammer.how: He leaps onto the marked spot and slams

linger.name: Cooling Slag
linger.how: Thrown hard, it slows to a stop and hangs in the air, cooling, before it crumbles

lines.t: Another order. Another blade. Step onto the anvil.
The floor plates begin to glow.
Too hot... Apprentices, the bellows!
Apprentices? ...Hm. You'll do.
The hammer does not miss. It only waits.
I forged these chains for prisoners. You'll fit.
The armor's off. Let the forge take the rest!

death.after: The hammer cools on the anvil. For the first time in a century, the forge-city is quiet.

bosses.name: The Pale Moth Matriarch
bosses.title: Mother of the Moonlit Glade
bosses.intro: Every moth in the Realm flies toward her light eventually. Very few fly back.

phases.name: Flutter
phases.text: She flies a figure eight, leaving a trail of hanging dust behind her and shedding swaying moths at you.
notes: The dust trail lingers: don't follow her path
Wing dust leaves you Blind: you can only see a few tiles around you for 2s

phases.name: Mesmer
phases.text: The eyes on her wings open. While they glow, moving toward her reverses your movement. Lunar scales curl out in flowers and moths sway in pairs.
notes: Back away or strafe: never walk at her while the eyes are open
The eyes close for 1s every 4s

phases.name: Chrysalis
phases.text: She wraps herself in a silk chrysalis with 8,000 HP. Break it within 10s or she emerges healed by 15%. The shell sheds scales and dust while you work.
notes: Everyone on the shell: this is a damage check

phases.name: Last Light
phases.text: Rage. The last light goes out of the glade except for three pools of moonlight drifting across the grass. Outside them, the dark drains you every half second. Stay in the light while the Matriarch fills it with moths.
notes: The pools wander, so move with yours
If two pools pass each other, switch to the one heading away from her

bosses.feel: Hypnotic. Swaying shots, hanging dust, and a gaze that turns you around.
signature: A trail of hanging dust
Mesmer: moving toward her reverses you
Chrysalis: break the shell in time
Moonbeam rings

dust.name: Moth Dust
dust.how: Hangs in the air where she flew. It gets in your eyes: Blind for 2s

scale.name: Lunar Scale
scale.how: Curls left and right in turn

lines.t: Little light, little light. Come closer.
Look at me. No, closer. Closer...
Hush now. Mother is changing.
My children all fly home to me. So will you!
The light dies, all but three pools of moonlight.

say.t: The moon is... so far tonight...

death.after: A thousand moths lift from the glade and scatter toward every lamp in the Realm.

bosses.name: Rime
bosses.title: The Glacier Heart
bosses.intro: The heart of a glacier that refused to melt, and grew a will to make sure it never would.

phases.name: Hail
phases.text: Hail. Frost orbits Rime. Rings of icicles freeze in mid-air, turn to face you, and fire. Frost bombs drift out slowly and burst into flakes.
notes: Frozen icicles all aim where you are when they thaw: move as they turn
Frost bombs burst at the same distance every time

phases.name: Snowfall
phases.text: A blizzard blows across the room at a slant. Snowstars drift out, stop, and shatter into icicles.
notes: Snowstars shatter in a fixed ring: back away the moment one stops

phases.name: Ice Pillars
phases.text: Pillars of ice burst from the floor around the room. They block shots in both directions, and after 4s each one shatters into a ring of icicles. Rime is untouchable while three or more stand.
notes: Use a pillar as cover from his icicles, then step away before it breaks

phases.name: Shatter
phases.text: Ice forms at the edges of the room and collapses inward toward Rime, while a two-armed icicle spiral turns.
notes: The inward ring has gaps: step through as it passes you

phases.name: Absolute Zero
phases.text: Rage. Frostbite builds on anyone who stands still for more than a second, freezing them for 1s. Rings of pinwheels and icicles alternate.
notes: Never stop moving, even to aim

bosses.feel: Cold geometry. Pinwheels, sideways snow and pillars that shatter.
signature: Orbiting pinwheel shards
A blizzard that blows sideways
Ice pillars that block, then shatter
Frostbite: stand still and you freeze

frost.name: Frost Pinwheel
frost.how: Spins around its path as it flies

pillar.name: Ice Pillar
pillar.how: Grows from the floor, blocks shots, shatters into icicles after 4s

hang.name: Hanging Icicle
hang.how: Freezes in mid-air for a second, turns to face you, then fires

frostbomb.name: Frost Bomb
frostbomb.how: A slow ball of frost that bursts into flakes after 5 tiles

lines.t: warmth detected.
correcting.
the wind obeys. the wind is cold.
stand still. become part of the glacier.
everything returns to the center. everything freezes.
no more motion. no more heat. no more you.

death.after: Drip. Drip. The Unmelting, for the first time in an age, begins to thaw.

bosses.name: Astraeus
bosses.title: The Fallen Star
bosses.intro: A star that fell into the Realm and took the shape of the knight it landed on.

phases.name: Constellation
phases.text: He dashes from star to star. Points of light appear and are joined into a constellation that becomes a laser after 1s, while curving starblades fly at you.
notes: Read the shape before it lights: you have 1.3s
A dotted line shows where he will dash 0.6s ahead
Falling blades start slow and accelerate: get clear early

phases.name: Starfall
phases.text: Meteors rain on the crater, each marked by a growing shadow. Impacts throw off starlight that sits still a moment, then streaks away, and leave a rock behind.
notes: Starlight is slow at first: get out of its line before it speeds up
Remember where the rocks land

phases.name: Supernova
phases.text: Astraeus goes supernova. Each nova is a ring of light with one gap: it expands to the edge of the crater, then collapses back into the star with its gap on the opposite side. Get through it going out, then again coming back.
notes: The gap flips to the far side on the way back: be ready to cross the room
Meteors still fall at random

phases.name: Collapse
phases.text: Rage. The fallen star collapses. Burning light creeps in from the rim of the crater, and the safe ground shrinks toward Astraeus as the phase goes on, so the fight gets closer and closer.
notes: The edge burns: stay inside the dark ring
The closer you're forced in, the less time you have to read each ring

bosses.feel: Cosmic. He dashes along lines of light and drags you toward him.
signature: Dashes between star points
Constellation lasers
Meteors that leave cover
Gravity that pulls you in

blade.name: Starblade
blade.how: Crescents that bend away from each other

meteor.name: Meteor
meteor.how: Its shadow grows for 1s, then it lands and leaves a rock

nova.name: Supernova
nova.how: A full ring of light. Only the rocks stop it

comet.name: Falling Blade
comet.how: Starts slow and gathers speed: it reaches you much faster than it left

lines.t: I fell for ten thousand years. Walk with me a little.
My siblings are still falling. Look up.
I will burn as I burned in the sky.
And then I will take it all back.
Everything falls toward me in the end. Even light.
The rim of the crater begins to burn inward.

say.t: Ah. So this is the ground.

death.after: What's left is a knight's armor cooling in the crater. The star is gone.

bosses.name: The Eclipse Twins
bosses.title: Lumen and Noct
bosses.intro: Sister of the sun and brother of the dark. Twice a century their moons cross, and they are at full strength.

phases.name: Day and Night
phases.text: The room splits in two. Left of the line is day, right is night, and the line drifts back and forth. Lumen's light only hurts you on the day side, Noct's shadow only on the night side. Shots that can't hurt you are see-through.
notes: Cross the line to shed one twin's attacks
The line moves on its own, so the safe side changes under you

phases.name: Orbit
phases.text: The twins circle each other, joined by a beam of light and shadow that sweeps the room as they orbit. Each one spins out a spiral as they go.
notes: The tether turns like a clock hand: step across it right behind it
It's shortest when they swing close together

phases.name: Totality
phases.text: They merge into the Eclipse, half sun and half shadow, slowly turning. Only shots that hit the bright half do damage. A corona of four beams of discs sweeps around them.
notes: Walk around with the bright side as it turns

phases.name: Separation
phases.text: Rage. They split again. Lumen and Noct each cast a beam from where they stand through the spot you were on, so the beams cross in an X there and pivot around it as they move. Noct charges and throws zigzagging stars. Kill both within 10s of each other or the survivor revives the other.
notes: Step off the X: the beams lock 1.1s before they fire
Noct marks his charge line 0.7s ahead

bosses.feel: Two fights at once. One slow and bright, one fast and dark.
signature: Shared health: damage them evenly
Opposing spirals in orbit
Totality: only the bright side can be hurt
Crossed beams through your position

ray.name: Sun and Shadow
ray.how: Two beams cross in an X over you

fang.name: Shadow Fang
fang.how: Noct. Fast and short; he keeps about 4 tiles away when he throws them

lines.t: Brother, we have guests.
Day for you. Night for me.
The room splits in two.
Round and round, little moth.
Mind the light between us.
The moons cross.
And we are whole.
You hurt her. You HURT her.
Together, brother. As always.

death.after: Two moons, one sky. They will rise again in a hundred years.

bosses.name: The Unmaker
bosses.title: The Eye Beneath
bosses.intro: Not a creature. A hole in the Realm that learned to look back.

phases.name: Gaze
phases.text: The eye watches the closest player. A line marks its beam a second before it fires. Void orbs swell, stall, then rush whoever they were aimed at.
notes: When an orb stalls, step sideways: it re-aims at your current spot

phases.name: Tear
phases.text: Rifts tear open across the floor and drag nearby players toward them. Tendrils writhe out toward you.
notes: Walk away from a rift before it fully opens
Void bolts Curse you: 25% more damage taken for 4s

phases.name: Reflection
phases.text: The eye opens wide every few seconds. While it's open, every shot you fire at it is reflected back at you. Null sparks ricochet around the room the whole time.
notes: Stop shooting the moment the eye opens; it stays open for 2s

phases.name: Singularity
phases.text: Rage. The Unmaker stops obeying space. Its shots blink: every 0.8s each one vanishes and reappears 2.2 tiles further along its path. A faint ring shows where it's about to land. The edges of the room collapse inward too: rings close in toward the singularity.
notes: Never stand where a ring appears
Between blinks they're slow, so the gaps are wider than they look
Closing rings come from the walls: watch behind you

bosses.feel: Wrongness. Things stall, ricochet, reflect and orbit.
signature: Orbs that stall and re-aim
Rifts that drag you in
Reflection: hold fire while the eye is open
Bullets caught in its orbit

void.name: Void Orb
void.how: Swells, stalls, then rushes you. Unmakes your defenses: Cursed, you take 25% more damage for 4s

tendril.name: Tendril
tendril.how: Writhes as it reaches for you

current.name: Event Horizon
current.how: Caught in its gravity: circles the eye as it drifts out

beam.name: Unmaking Beam
beam.how: Telegraphed laser; in rage two of them rotate

rift.name: Rift
rift.how: Opens on the floor and pulls you in

blink.name: Blinking Null
blink.how: Every 0.8s it vanishes and reappears 2.2 tiles further on. A ring shows where it will land

lines.t: I SEE YOU.
THERE IS A PLACE WHERE YOU WERE NOT.
I AM MAKING IT.
WHAT YOU GIVE, I RETURN. WHAT YOU ARE, I TAKE.
ALL THINGS END.
Its shots begin to skip through space.

death.after: The rift seals with a sound like a door closing in another room.

bosses.name: The Cantor
bosses.title: Conductor of the Drowned Choir
bosses.intro: The chapel sank during the evening hymn. The choirmaster never let them stop singing.

phases.name: Prelude
phases.text: The Cantor lays a stave across the chapel: five long lines from wall to wall. Notes slide along them in time with the music. A line lights up 0.7s before a note slides down it, from the side the arrow points.
notes: Stand between the lines, not on them
Two lines light at once, never the same line twice in a row

phases.name: Downbeat
phases.text: The choir takes over the tempo. He can only be damaged on the downbeat, the fourth beat of every bar, when he glows. Pearls go out on every beat and a hymn burst on the downbeat.
notes: Count 1-2-3-hit
Shots that land off-beat do nothing

phases.name: High Tide
phases.text: High tide. Curtains of water sweep down the chapel, each with one gap, and the gap swings from one side of you to the other with every wave. A beam of light sweeps the floor and pearls roll along the walls.
notes: The gaps alternate left, right, left: start moving toward the next one before the wave arrives
Don't hug the walls: pearls roll along them

phases.name: Fugue
phases.text: A four-beat phrase that repeats: a pearl ring, a hymn burst, a fan of bouncing notes, then one beat of rest.
notes: The rest beat is your time to reposition

phases.name: Requiem of the Deep
phases.text: Rage. A three-armed spiral of hymn waves, pearls on every beat, and notes bouncing everywhere.
notes: The spiral never changes speed

bosses.feel: Rhythm. Everything lands on the beat.
signature: Every attack on the beat
Downbeat: he can only be hurt on beat four
Tides that sweep sideways
A lighthouse beam that turns a full circle

pearl.name: Pearl
pearl.how: Fired on the beat. In High Tide they spray from the tip of the lighthouse beam

tide.name: Tide
tide.how: A wall of water that sweeps sideways

light.name: Lighthouse Beam
light.how: Turns a full circle around him like a lighthouse; reaches 5.5 tiles

staffnote.name: Staff Note
staffnote.how: Slides along one of the five lines of the staff, straight through the walls

lines.t: Places, everyone. From the top.
Five lines of a stave stretch across the chapel.
One, two, three, AND—
The tide keeps better time than any of you.
Again! We do not stop until it is perfect.
Sing! SING! The sea is listening!

death.after: The singing stops. Somewhere in the deep, one voice keeps humming the last bar.

bosses.name: Elderbark
bosses.title: The Oathroot
bosses.intro: An oak that swore to guard the grove, and kept its oath long after the grove forgot it.

phases.name: The Oath
phases.text: Elderbark binds you to its oath. A vine runs from the oak to you, and if you stray more than 6.5 tiles away it pulls you back and the thorns bite. Fight it up close while leaves spiral out from the branches.
notes: The dashed circle is the length of the vine
Close in, its leaves are densest: use the circle's edge

phases.name: Briar Hedges
phases.text: Thorn hedges grow across the grove, carving it into lanes that last 4s. The spirit of the Hollow Stag charges down a lane every few seconds.
notes: Hedges sprout for 0.9s before they turn solid
A glowing lane marks the stag's charge 1s before it comes

phases.name: Seedfall
phases.text: Seeds rain down on marked spots. Each one that lands sprouts a sapling, and saplings shed rings of leaves every few seconds until they wither 8s later. The grove fills up with little trees.
notes: Saplings stay 8s: don't get boxed in between them
Fight near the oldest ones; they'll be gone first

phases.name: Roots
phases.text: Roots. Two great roots sweep slowly around Elderbark like the hands of a clock. Keep walking around the tree ahead of them while thorns ring outward.
notes: The roots turn steadily: circle in the same direction and stay between them
They only reach 9 tiles: the far edges of the grove are safe from them

phases.name: Uprooted
phases.text: Rage. He tears himself free and walks. Defense drops to 20, but saplings sprout behind him and heal him while they live.
notes: Kill saplings on sight; he's slow enough to kite in a big circle

bosses.feel: An unmovable wall that slowly fills the grove.
signature: Regenerates until the braziers burn
Thorn hedges and the charging stag
Roots that march toward you
Saplings that heal him

seed.name: Seed Bomb
seed.how: Slows down and bursts into 8 thorns

root.name: Root Eruption
root.how: Roots burst up in a line toward you

hedge.name: Thorn Hedge
hedge.how: Grows across the grove and lasts 4s

stag.name: Hollow Stag
stag.how: A spirit that charges down a lane

seedfall.name: Falling Seed
seedfall.how: Lands where it's marked, then sprouts a sapling that sheds leaves

lash.name: Root Lash
lash.how: Two great roots sweep slowly around the tree. Walk around with them

lines.t: I swore to keep this grove. I keep my word.
A vine wraps around your ankle. You are bound to the oath.
Thorn and briar, rise. The grove is closed.
Every seed is a promise. Every promise grows.
My roots run under all of it.
You are standing on my oath.
Then I will break the earth to keep it!

say.t: The oath... passes... to the seed...

death.after: Where he fell, a single sapling pushes up through the moss.

bosses.name: Tempest Roc
bosses.title: Eye of the Storm
bosses.intro: A bird the size of a ship, nesting in the thunderheads. Lightning follows it like gulls follow a boat.

phases.name: Gale
phases.text: The Roc circles the peak. The wind pushes everyone clockwise, fans of feathers bend in it, and single bolts snap at you.
notes: Lean against the wind or you'll drift into the fans

phases.name: Thunderhead
phases.text: Thunderhead. Lightning arcs across the room in a grid of parallel lines, alternating between rows and columns. One line near you is always left dark: get onto it before the grid strikes.
notes: The lines glow for 1.25s first
The safe lane is always the one you're standing nearest to: find it and hold still

phases.name: Eye of the Storm
phases.text: Two columns of rising wind drift across the summit. Inside one you're lifted toward the Roc and shots are carried upward. Feathers spiral out of the eye of the storm around it.
notes: You can still walk out of a column, just slowly upward
Shots slow down inside a column when they're falling toward you

phases.name: Downburst
phases.text: Rage. It climbs out of sight, then dives across the peak through your position, firing bolts on every pass.
notes: A red line marks each dive 0.8s ahead: move sideways off it
It can't be hurt above the clouds, only on the dive and while it circles back

bosses.feel: Speed. It never stops moving and neither can you.
signature: Wind that pushes you
Lightning that strikes where you're going
Storm walls that turn
Dives from the sky

bolt.name: Bolt
bolt.how: The fastest shot in the fight

gust.name: Gust
gust.how: Starts slow, then speeds up and spreads

strike.name: Lightning Strike
strike.how: Strikes where you will be in 0.9s

arc.name: Lightning Grid
arc.how: Lightning arcs across the room in parallel lines. One line near you never strikes

lines.t: The Tempest Roc screeches, and the wind turns with it.
Thunder rolls. The Roc's eyes flash white.
The Roc settles into the eye of the storm.
Columns of wind start to rise across the summit.
The Roc climbs out of sight. The air goes very still.

say.t: The Tempest Roc gives one last screech and falls.

death.after: The storm breaks. For the first time in years, there is sun on the peaks.

bosses.name: Ignis
bosses.title: The Undying Phoenix
bosses.intro: It has died a thousand times and come back each time a little hotter. It has three lives left in it today.

phases.name: Kindling
phases.text: Ignis sets the ground alight. Fires catch near you and spread in random directions, each flame lighting two more, three generations deep, before they burn out after 3s.
notes: Move away from a new fire early: it grows outward
Old fires burn out first, so the patch behind a fire is soon safe again

phases.name: Ashes
phases.text: It collapses into an egg circled by three flame wisps while embers rain on the peak. Kill all three wisps within 8s or it hatches with its life fully restored.
notes: The wisps orbit fast: lead your shots

phases.name: Blaze
phases.text: Faster and hotter. It circles the peak leaving burning ground, turns a three-armed feather spiral, and sends rings of fire pillars rippling outward from itself.
notes: Each ring fires 0.45s after the one inside it, with gaps of 1–4 tiles between pillars and a tile of safe ground between rings
Step into a gap in the next ring, or through a ring right after it fires

phases.name: The Ninth Sun
phases.text: Rage. Ignis becomes the Ninth Sun. Sunspots drift slowly across the floor and burn anyone standing in one. A spiral of accelerating sunbursts and fans of feathers fill the gaps.
notes: Watch the floor as much as the bullets

bosses.feel: Escalation. It keeps coming back hotter.
signature: Three lives
An egg guarded by flame wisps
Pillars that ripple out from it
Sunspots that drift across the floor

pillar.name: Fire Pillar
pillar.how: Erupts in rings that ripple outward from Ignis

wisp.name: Flame Wisp
wisp.how: Circles the egg. Kill all three before it hatches (2,000 HP)

lines.t: Nine hundred and ninety-seven deaths. Shall we make it ninety-eight?
The ground catches fire.
Death is only a door.
I know the way back.
Hotter! Every life, hotter!
Behold the Ninth Sun!
Burn with me!

death.after: Only ash remains. Something in it is still warm.

bosses.name: The Ashen Cardinal
bosses.title: Last Priest of the Burned Cathedral
bosses.intro: He was leading the evening mass when the fire came. He finished it anyway.

phases.name: Procession
phases.text: The procession. The Cardinal walks his aisle with four censers swinging around him on chains, and slashes in wide fans.
notes: The censers circle close to him: keep your distance and they can't reach you

phases.name: Stained Glass
phases.text: The windows shatter and colored light falls across the nave in moving shafts. His censer burns one color at a time, and only players standing in light of that color can hurt him. Glass shards fall, stop, and fly at you.
notes: Watch the censer's color, then find that shaft
The color changes every 4s

phases.name: Ashfall
phases.text: Ash drifts from the roof and settles into clouds that blind and burn. He keeps walking the aisle, slashing in wide fans.
notes: Wait out the clouds rather than walking through
The ash gets in your eyes: walking through a cloud leaves you Blind for 2s

phases.name: Requiem
phases.text: Rage. The organ plays. On every chord, a row of pipes bursts up from the floor across the nave. Rings of slashes go out on each note and the censer keeps streaming.
notes: Each chord skips one column, always within two columns of you
The columns glow for 1.9s first: the dark one is safe

bosses.feel: Ceremony. A slow procession, colored light and an organ that won't stop.
signature: Walks the aisle swinging a censer
Stained glass: match his color to hurt him
Ash clouds that blind
Organ pipes that erupt from the floor

glass.name: Stained Glass
glass.how: Falls, stops, then flies at you

pipe.name: Organ Pipe
pipe.how: Columns that burst up from the floor on each chord, 1.9s after they glow

censer.name: Censer
censer.how: Swung on a chain around the Cardinal

lines.t: Rise for the procession.
Let the windows speak.
Stand in the right light, child.
Ash to the faithful. Ash to all.
The organ, please. The mass is not over.

death.after: The mass is ended. The candles go out one by one.

bosses.name: Sarrukh
bosses.title: The Dunesea Wyrm
bosses.intro: A worm long enough to circle the oasis twice. It has been swimming under the dunes since before the desert was a desert.

phases.name: The Hunt
phases.text: Sarrukh surfaces and hunts. Its body follows its head in a long curve, and every segment throws grit off its sides as it passes. The maw spits fans of sand at you.
notes: The body is the danger: never let yourself get boxed between head and tail
Grit only flies sideways from the body, so cross it end-on

phases.name: Burrow
phases.text: It dives. A ripple in the sand chases you for a second, then locks, and the Wyrm erupts from that spot throwing a ring of grit. Scarabs dig up from the sand between eruptions.
notes: When the ripple stops following you, step out: you have 0.7s
It can't be hurt while it's underground
Scarabs tunnel toward you as ripples in the sand, then burst up when they're close

phases.name: Sandstorm
phases.text: A sandstorm rolls over the oasis. You can only see a few tiles around you, sand drives across the room at a slant, and the Wyrm circles the edge of the storm.
notes: Every shot still glows through the sand: watch for shapes, not colors
The body circles the rim, so the middle is safest

phases.name: Coil
phases.text: It coils around the middle of the oasis and spins. Every segment fires straight out from the coil, so the body becomes a turning wheel of sand with gaps between the spokes.
notes: Stand in a gap between spokes and turn with the coil
The head still spits at you from inside the wheel

phases.name: Glass Fury
phases.text: Rage. Lightning splits the sky over the dunes. Where it lands the sand fuses into glass that shatters outward, while the Wyrm hunts at full speed.
notes: The bolts land where you are going: change direction when one is marked ahead of you

bosses.feel: A hunt. A body that fills the arena, and a head that comes up from under your feet.
signature: A body of nine segments that all shoot
Burrows and erupts under you
A sandstorm that hides the room
Coils into a turning wheel of sand

spit.name: Sand Spit
spit.how: Spat from the maw in fans

grit.name: Grit
grit.how: Thrown sideways off the body segments

grain.name: Sand Grain
grain.how: Driven across the room by the sandstorm

shard.name: Glass Shard
shard.how: Sand fused to glass where lightning strikes

seg.name: Wyrm Segment
seg.how: Part of the body. Touching it hurts

scarab.name: Sand Scarab
scarab.how: Digs up from the sand and scuttles at you, then bursts into grit

erupt.name: Eruption
erupt.how: The Wyrm bursts up from below. The ripple locks 0.7s before it does

strike.name: Glassing Bolt
strike.how: Lightning that fuses the sand to glass where you are about to be

lines.t: The ground hums. Something enormous is moving under the sand.
Sarrukh dives. The sand begins to ripple toward you.
A sandstorm rolls over the oasis.
Somewhere inside it, the Wyrm is circling.
Sarrukh coils around the oasis and begins to spin.
Lightning splits the sky. Where it lands, the sand turns to glass.

say.t: Sarrukh rears up, shudders, and crashes back into the sand.

death.after: The dunes go quiet. For the first time in centuries, the oasis is still.

bosses.name: The Brass Magistrate
bosses.title: Arbiter of the Final Hour
bosses.intro: A clockwork judge built to hear every case the Realm ever brought. It has been in session for four hundred years, and every defendant has been found guilty.

phases.name: Order in the Court
phases.text: Order in the court! Every few seconds the gavel falls, and anyone moving when it lands is struck down and stunned for a moment. Between strikes, dodge the hands of the clock and the ticking rings.
notes: A gold ring fills around the Magistrate before each strike: stop moving when it closes
Standing still is safe from the gavel, not from the shots

phases.name: Time Stop
phases.text: It stops time. Every few seconds the clock strikes and every shot in the room freezes for 1.4s while the Magistrate keeps firing. You can still move. When time starts again, everything moves at once.
notes: Time Stop doesn't affect you: use the freeze to walk to an empty spot
The clock chimes 0.7s before each stop

phases.name: Rewind
phases.text: Everything it fires comes back. Ticks fly out and rewind; mainsprings curl out in loops and retrace them backwards. The court fills with patterns that are about to reverse.
notes: Watch the path a shot has taken: that's where it's going next

phases.name: The Pendulum
phases.text: The great pendulum of the court swings below the bench. Time bombs tick down across the floor, and cogs ricochet off the walls.
notes: Step across the pendulum right after it passes you
A bomb's clock hand shows how long you have

phases.name: Final Verdict
phases.text: Rage. The verdict is in. Time stops more often, the gavel falls on you, ticks rewind, and cogs roll out of every slam.
notes: Use each Time Stop to get out from under the next gavel

bosses.feel: Control. It stops time, rewinds its own shots and swings the court's great pendulum.
signature: Time Stop: every shot freezes, you don't
Shots that rewind back along their path
The court's great pendulum
Gears that roll off the walls

cog.name: Cog
cog.how: Rolls and ricochets off the walls

tick.name: Tick
tick.how: Flies out for 0.8s, then rewinds back along its path

spring.name: Mainspring
spring.how: Curls out in a loop, then rewinds the same loop backwards

gavel.name: Gavel
gavel.how: Slams where you stand after 1.2s and rolls cogs out

bomb.name: Time Bomb
bomb.how: A clock face counts down 2.2s, then detonates

pendulum.name: Great Pendulum
pendulum.how: Swings 140° back and forth below the bench

lines.t: Court is now in session.
The accused will rise.
The court will have silence.
And stillness.
Strike that from the record.
Let us try that again.
The sentence is time.
All of it.
The verdict is in.
GUILTY.

death.after: The great clock stops. Somewhere in the archive, a case file closes itself.

bosses.name: Vitrea
bosses.title: The Thousandfold
bosses.intro: A queen made of glass, standing in a hall made of mirrors. Nobody has ever been sure which one of her is real, and that includes Vitrea.

phases.name: Mirror Image
phases.text: Vitrea and her reflection move as one, mirrored across the hall. Everything she fires, the reflection fires too, and two tall mirrors on the walls bounce shots back into the room.
notes: The reflection always stands opposite her: if she's on the left, it's on the right
A shot that hits a mirror comes back at the same angle, so watch the walls

phases.name: Echoes
phases.text: Three reflections now, and they're late. One copies her 0.6s after she moves, one 1.2s after, and the third does something of its own: it spins out a spiral. A prism at the bottom of the hall splits any bolt that hits it.
notes: Each attack arrives three times, one after another. Dodge the first, then expect the echoes
The spinning reflection never copies her. It's the one firing the spiral

phases.name: Fracture
phases.text: The hall starts to break. New panes of glass grow out of the floor, every hit cracks them, and a pane that breaks throws shards and splits in two. Her Lightray is aimed at you and ricochets off every mirror in its way.
notes: The Lightray's warning line already shows its bounces: read the whole path, not just the first segment
Breaking panes thins the maze but spits shards: break them when you're not standing next to them

phases.name: The Thousandfold
phases.text: Eight Vitreas circle the hall and all of them attack. Only one is real. The real one casts a shadow and isn't mirrored; the reflections are flipped and have no shadow. Shoot a reflection and it breaks and fires back at you. Hit the real one 16 times and every reflection shatters, then they all shuffle.
notes: Look for the shadow under her feet, and which way her hand mirror is held
Wrong guesses cost you: a broken reflection throws a fan of slivers at you
After each shuffle she flashes. Find her again before you shoot

phases.name: Shatterpoint
phases.text: Rage. Everything at once: delayed reflections, prisms that split every bolt, panes growing and shattering, and the Lightray bouncing through all of it.
notes: Stay near the middle: the edges are where reflected shots stack up

bosses.feel: Confusion that stays readable. Copies of her fire with her, panes of glass bend your shots and hers, and eventually you have to pick the real one out of eight.
signature: Reflections that copy her attacks, some on a delay
Panes of glass that bounce, split and bend shots
A light beam that ricochets around the hall
Eight Vitreas, one of them real

prism.name: Prism Bolt
prism.how: Bounces off mirrors. A prism splits it into two shards

sliver.name: Glass Sliver
sliver.how: A thin, fast splinter, often thrown in fans

lightray.name: Lightray
lightray.how: A beam aimed at you that ricochets off every mirror in its path

lines.t: Look at me.
No. Look at ME.
Her reflections start to lag behind her.
Which of us did you mean to hit?
You're breaking my hall.
Every piece of it is still me.
Eight Vitreas step out of the glass.
Find the real Vitrea: she casts a shadow and isn't mirrored.
Choose.
If I break, which of us is left?
Not you.

death.after: Every mirror in the hall goes dark at once. For the first time, the room reflects nothing.

bosses.name: Abbot Ossian
bosses.title: The Unmoored
bosses.intro: Ossian meditated on weightlessness for sixty years, until one morning the mountain monastery agreed with him and let go of the ground. Now it hangs upside down in the sky, and so does he.

phases.name: Prayer Stones
phases.text: Two prayer stones swing around the abbot on their chains. Each one has its own weight: shots passing near them curve, anything that reaches one is swallowed, and standing close pulls you in.
notes: A stone between you and the abbot is a shield: his shots bend around it or fall in
Rings come out round and arrive bent, so the gaps move

phases.name: The Bell Tolls
phases.text: The great bell tolls and the monastery turns over. Every 4s the whole room falls in a new direction: down, left, up, right. Shots fall with it, and so do you. An arrow at the top of the arena shows which way is down next.
notes: Walking against the fall is slower; walking with it is faster
Shots curve toward the current 'down', so their gaps open on the uphill side

phases.name: Unmoored
phases.text: The last of the weight lets go. Your input now accelerates you instead of moving you: release the keys and you keep drifting until you push the other way. The abbot lays incense across the path you're drifting along and drops stones where you'll be, not where you are.
notes: To stop, push the opposite way. Tap, don't hold
His traps assume you'll keep drifting, so change course early
The line in front of you shows your speed and direction

phases.name: Breath of the Mountain
phases.text: The abbot breathes, and the mountain breathes with him. Every 3s a gust of weight pushes out from him, shoving you away, and the next one draws you back in. At the edges of the floor, the wind off the drop tears at you.
notes: Watch the REPEL / ATTRACT warning and lean against it before it lands
A push near the edge throws you into the wind: stay toward the middle

phases.name: The Fall
phases.text: Rage. The sky tears open under the monastery. The tear circles the abbot, pulling hard across most of the room and swallowing every shot that reaches it, while spirals of prayer beads curve into its wake.
notes: Keep moving away from the tear: its pull is strongest close in
It eats shots, so the far side of it is the safest place in the room

bosses.feel: Weight. Prayer stones bend your shots, the monastery turns over when the bell tolls, and then the last of the weight goes and every move you make keeps going.
signature: Prayer stones on chains that bend shots and pull you
The great bell tolls and the monastery turns: down changes direction
Unmoored: you drift until you push back
The sky tears open beneath the monastery

bead.name: Prayer Bead
bead.how: Light enough that every prayer stone bends it

stone.name: Falling Stone
stone.how: Fast and aimed. Unmoored, it's aimed where your drift is taking you

incense.name: Incense
incense.how: Slow puffs. Unmoored, they're laid across the path you're drifting along

censer.name: Swinging Censer
censer.how: Drifts after you on its broken chain, then bursts into prayer beads

boulder.name: Prayer Stone
boulder.how: A boulder on a chain. Bends every shot near it and pulls you gently in

bellwell.name: Loose Bell
bellwell.how: A small bell that drifts around the room while you're Unmoored, pulling on everything

abyss.name: The Tear
abyss.how: A hole in the sky. Pulls hard, and swallows any shot that reaches it

lines.t: The abbot opens his eyes. His prayer stones begin to swing.
Let go.
The great bell tolls. The monastery turns over.
Down is only a habit.
The last of the weight lets go. You start to drift.
Unmoored: your input accelerates you. Push the other way to stop.
Nothing stops. It only changes course.
Breathe in.
Breathe out.
Wind howls up from the drop at the edges.
The sky tears open beneath the monastery.
Fall with me.

death.after: The prayer stones fall still. Somewhere far below, the monastery's shadow settles back onto the mountain, and every bell rings once.

bosses.name: Aion
bosses.title: Keeper of the Still Hour
bosses.intro: Aion keeps the hour that never ends, the moment between one tick and the next. Inside it everything stops, except you.

phases.name: The First Hour

puzzle.say: TIME STOPS. Shatter the Hour Crystals before it resumes!
puzzle.win: Every crystal shattered. Aion's shield falls!
puzzle.lose: A crystal survived. It bursts into sand.

phases.text: Aion's shield can't be broken by damage. Every 7s the Still Hour begins: everything freezes except you, and Hour Crystals appear around the room. Shoot them all before time resumes and the shield drops for 4s. Miss one and it bursts into a ring of sand.
notes: Frozen shots still hurt if you walk into them: plan a path through the freeze
One more crystal appears every Still Hour

phases.name: The Sundial

puzzle.goal: Push the Sun Disc into the socket
puzzle.say: TIME STOPS. Roll the Sun Disc into the sundial's socket!
puzzle.win: The sundial catches the light. A sunbeam burns through Aion!
puzzle.lose: The disc stays dark, and bursts.

phases.text: A Sun Disc appears somewhere in the room when time stops. Walk into it to push it, and steer it into the socket below the sundial. When time resumes, the sundial fires a sunbeam that burns away every shot in its path and drops Aion's shield.
notes: Push from the far side: the disc moves away from you
The disc starts further from the socket each round

phases.name: The Ordering of Hours

puzzle.goal: Step on the runes in order: I, II, III
puzzle.say: TIME STOPS. Step on the runes in the order they're numbered!
puzzle.win: The runes ring in order. The shield falls!
puzzle.lose: The sequence breaks. The runes erupt.

phases.text: Runes light up on the floor, each with a numeral. Step on them in order during the Still Hour. Get one wrong and the sequence breaks: when time resumes, every rune erupts in a pillar of light.
notes: The numerals are shuffled every round: read before you run
Don't stand on a rune when a broken sequence resumes

phases.name: Turning the Sun

puzzle.goal: Push the mirror onto the golden mark
puzzle.say: TIME STOPS. Aion's Sun Lances hang in the air. Push the mirror into their path!
puzzle.win: The lances strike the mirror and turn on their maker!

phases.text: When time stops, Aion has just fired a line of Sun Lances at you. They hang frozen. Push the hand mirror onto the golden mark in their path, then get out of the line. When time resumes, the lances hit the mirror and fly back into Aion.
notes: The golden mark is the end of the lance line. Park the mirror there, then step aside
If you don't, the lances keep going toward where you were standing

phases.name: The Last Hour

puzzle.goal: Shatter the crystals AND step on the runes in order
puzzle.say: TIME STOPS. Crystals and runes, all before the hour turns!
puzzle.win: The Last Hour breaks. Aion is exposed!

phases.text: Rage. Every Still Hour is crystals and runes at once, with less combat time between them, while Aion fills the room with sand and hour hands.
notes: Shoot crystals on the way to each rune: you don't have time to do them separately

bosses.feel: Puzzles under fire. Its shield can't be broken by damage alone. Time stops on a schedule, and what you do while it's stopped decides what happens next.
signature: The Still Hour: time stops for everything but you
Shatter crystals, dock the sun disc, step on runes in order
Push a mirror into frozen lances to turn them on Aion
Fail and the puzzle turns on you

sand.name: Hour Sand
sand.how: Grains of time, thrown in rings and spirals

hourhand.name: Hour Hand
hourhand.how: A fast hand off the clock, aimed at you

lance.name: Sun Lance
lance.how: Fired in a line at the start of the Still Hour, frozen until time resumes. Redirect them with the mirror

rune.name: Rune Pillar
rune.how: Erupts from the runes when the sequence is broken

glyph.name: Hour Glyph
glyph.how: A circle of light that bursts into sand

crystal.name: Hour Crystal
crystal.how: Appears in the Still Hour. Shoot it 4 times to shatter it. Any left when time resumes burst into sand

sundisc.name: Sun Disc
sundisc.how: Push it into the sundial's socket during the Still Hour and a sunbeam burns through Aion

tmirror.name: Hand Mirror
tmirror.how: Push it onto the golden mark in front of the frozen lances to turn them around

lines.t: Between this moment and the next, there is a door.
Aion's shield can't be broken by damage. Solve the Still Hour to expose it.
The sun must sit in its socket.
Put it back.
Hours have an order.
Walk them as they were walked.
You stand in the path of my sun.
Will you turn it?
This is the Last Hour.
There is no next one.

say.t: Go. Time is waiting for you.

death.after: The sand in every hourglass falls at once. Outside, the priests stand up and stretch, as if they had only knelt a moment.

bosses.name: Vael
bosses.title: The Starbound Huntress
bosses.intro: A hunter so good the sky kept her. She was drawn into the stars as a constellation, and she has been hunting across the night ever since.

phases.name: Hunter's Mark
phases.text: Vael circles the room and marks you. A golden reticle follows you for a second, then locks and turns red. Half a second later six star arrows fly in from all around the mark and meet in the middle.
notes: When the reticle turns red, it stops following: just walk out of it
The dashed lines show where the arrows come from

phases.name: Comet Hounds
phases.text: She looses her hounds. Each one runs you down, crouches with its lunge line showing, and pounces across the room. Vael covers them with scatter arrows that burst into stardust.
notes: When a hound crouches, step off its dashed line: it can't turn once it jumps
Scatter arrows burst 6.5 tiles out, so stay close or stay far

phases.name: Starflight
phases.text: The floor falls away and the chase goes out into the stars. Stars stream out of the distance in every direction. While a star is see-through it's still far away and can't hurt you; it turns solid once it's close enough to hit. Now and then a shooting star breaks from the pack much faster. Every few seconds a slow star gate comes: a golden wedge shows where its gap will be, then the ring follows with the gap edged in gold.
notes: See-through stars are harmless. Only solid ones can hit you
Every star moves straight out from the middle, so dodge sideways around the centre
Shooting stars are faint for longer: spot them early
The next gate gap is never far from the last one

phases.name: Moonlit Ambush
phases.text: Back in the Atlas, Vael vanishes and reappears somewhere else in the room every few seconds, firing a ring of arrows each time she lands. A hound hunts with her, and the Hunter's Mark keeps finding you.
notes: Each landing fires a ring: keep some distance from where she might appear
When the reticle turns red, walk out of it

phases.name: Supernova Run
phases.text: Rage. Starflight again: more stars, more shooting stars, gates more often, and every so often the Hunter's Mark follows you through the stars.
notes: Head for the gate early, then dodge the solid stars on the way
When the reticle turns red, step out of it

bosses.feel: Being hunted. She marks you, sends her comet hounds after you, vanishes into the dark, and then the floor falls away and the chase goes out into the stars.
signature: The Hunter's Mark: a reticle locks on, then arrows converge on it
Comet hounds that close in, crouch and lunge
Starflight: a chase through the cosmos
Gates of stars with a golden gap to fly through

star.name: Star
star.how: A small, bright point of light
