starrow.name: Star Arrow
starrow.how: Fired from her star bow in fans

splitarrow.name: Scatter Arrow
splitarrow.how: Flies 6.5 tiles, then bursts into a ring of stardust

astral.name: Oncoming Star
astral.how: In Starflight, stars start far ahead and rush past, growing as they come. While a star is see-through it can't hurt you; once it turns solid it can

astralfast.name: Shooting Star
astralfast.how: Every so often a star breaks from the pack and streaks at you much faster. It's faint until it's close, so watch for it early

astralring.name: Ring Star
astralring.how: The stars of a star gate. They come slowly, in a full ring with one gap

astralgate.name: Gate Star
astralgate.how: The golden stars on either side of the gap in a star gate. A golden wedge shows where the gap is coming

dust.name: Stardust
dust.how: Bursts out of scatter arrows and dying hounds

hound.name: Comet Hound
hound.how: Runs you down, crouches with a dashed line showing its lunge, then pounces. Bursts into stardust

lines.t: Every star is a trail.
And you are on all of them.
A golden reticle settles over you.
Hounds. Fetch.
Comet hounds bound out of the sky.
The floor falls away. You're flying through the stars.
Starflight: see-through stars can't hurt you yet. Fly through the gold gap in each star gate.
Keep up.
The stars settle. Vael is gone.
Where am I, little quarry?
Run, then. The sky is endless.
Vael takes flight again, faster.

say.t: No one has kept up... in a thousand years.

death.after: Vael's stars drift apart, one by one, and settle back into the sky. Somewhere above the Atlas, a new constellation is missing a hunter.

bosses.name: King Morvane
bosses.title: The Hollow Crown
bosses.intro: Morvane traded his heart for a crown that would never let him die. It kept its word. Inside the armor there is nothing left but the crown, and it still wants a kingdom.

phases.name: The Throne Room
phases.text: The king holds court from his throne. Ranks of royal guards march out from him four abreast, straight at where you stood, decrees fly at your head, and the ghosts of his old subjects drift after you.
notes: A rank marches in a straight line: step around its end
Shades are slow but they follow you

phases.name: Checkmate
phases.text: The floor becomes a chessboard. Pieces appear near you and strike in their own patterns: a rook along its row and column, a bishop along the diagonals, a queen along all four, and a knight on every square an L-jump away.
notes: Look at which piece it is before you move: each one has a different set of safe squares
Against a knight, stand next to it. Its leap can't hit adjacent squares

phases.name: The King's Gambit
phases.text: Morvane sets out a chess problem in the middle of the hall and dares you to solve it: white to move, checkmate in one. Your piece glows gold and its possible moves are marked. Walk onto the square you want to move to and stand there to play it. Find the mate and the Black King shatters, staggering Morvane. Play the wrong move, or run out of time, and every black piece on the board strikes along its lines. A new problem is drawn at random each time.
notes: Read the whole position before you move: the black pieces block the king's escape squares
Only the marked squares count, and you have 9 seconds
Stand clear of the black pieces' rows and files if you miss

phases.name: Chandeliers
phases.text: Morvane cuts the chandeliers loose. Their shadows grow on the floor before they land, and each one shatters into decrees. He throws his crown at you, and it comes back.
notes: The crown comes back along the same line, so step off it twice

phases.name: The Black Court
phases.text: His whole court rises. Six shadow courtiers stand around the edge of the hall and throw decrees at you, each on its own beat, while ranks of guards march through the middle.
notes: Every courtier aims at you, so keep moving and the decrees cross behind you
Put a marching rank between you and the courtiers

phases.name: Hollow Crown
phases.text: Rage. The Hollow Crown leaves its king. It circles the throne room on its own, throwing decrees from wherever it is, while Morvane's pieces keep striking across the board.
notes: Track the crown: its decrees come from a moving point
The chess lines still show in red first

bosses.feel: Cruel order. The throne room turns into a chessboard and his pieces strike in their own patterns. Then the candles go out.
signature: The floor becomes a chessboard: rooks, bishops, queens and knights strike in their own lines
Royal guards who march on you
Falling chandeliers
Solve his chess problems: find the mate in one

decree.name: Royal Decree
decree.how: A blade of red seal-wax, aimed at you

crown.name: Thrown Crown
crown.how: Flies out and comes back to his hand

shade.name: Shade
shade.how: A slow ghost of a former subject that drifts after you

royal.name: Checkmate
royal.how: A chess piece appears on the board and strikes along its lines: rook straight, bishop diagonal, queen both

pike.name: Knight's Leap
pike.how: A knight piece strikes every square an L-shaped jump away

chandelier.name: Chandelier
chandelier.how: Cut loose from the ceiling. It shatters into decrees when it lands

guard.name: Royal Guard
guard.how: An empty suit of armor that marches at you, then bursts into decrees

lines.t: Kneel.
Everyone kneels, eventually.
You are a pawn on my board.
Pawns are spent first.
Do you play, peasant?
A chess problem appears on the floor of the hall.
White to move: checkmate in one. Stand on the right square.
Light the hall for my guest.
Morvane cuts the chandelier ropes.
Rise, my court.
Shadow courtiers take their places around the hall.
The crown lifts from Morvane's head and takes flight.
The crown is the kingdom.

death.after: The armor folds in on itself. The crown rolls across the floor, rattles to a stop, and for the first time in centuries, nobody is wearing it.

bosses.name: Lord Gourdrick
bosses.title: The Pumpkin Lord
bosses.intro: Every autumn the Pumpkin Lord grows a little bigger and the patch a little wider. This year he reached the border of the Melon Kingdom, and the Kingdom sent its two best.

phases.name: The Patch
phases.text: Your friends fight from the sidelines. Sir Rindley holds the left edge of the patch: every few seconds he charges the Lord, and every 8s he hurls his Rind Shield, which circles you for 3.5s and blocks any shot it touches. Sister Honeydew holds the right edge and sends a beam of healing to you every 6s, wherever you are. The Lord throws seeds at everyone and curls vines at the knight.
notes: Fight hardest while the Rind Shield is circling you
Honeydew's heal reaches you anywhere, so you're free to dodge

phases.name: Snare
phases.text: The Lord snares Sir Rindley in vines. While he's caught he can't block anything and takes damage every second. Shoot the vines ten times to free him, and he staggers the Lord with a charge. Wait too long and Rindley goes down for a while.
notes: Your shots go to the vines automatically while he's snared
Freeing him stops the Lord's attacks for 3s

phases.name: Harvest Moon
phases.text: The Lord calls down the Harvest Moon. Every 10s Sister Honeydew casts a dome of light near you from the sideline, and the sky outside it starts to burn. Get inside before the 3s countdown ends. Everything outside the dome takes 380, and the Moon burns away every shot that's inside the dome.
notes: The dome always appears a couple of tiles from you, toward the middle
Jack-o'-lanterns roll after you, so don't lead them into the dome

phases.name: Rotten Harvest
phases.text: The Lord curses Sister Honeydew and she collapses. Stand beside her for a little over 2s to break the curse: she heals you for 250 and the Lord staggers. Leave her too long and the curse bursts out of her as rot, and she stays down.
notes: She collapses where she stands on the right edge, so the run to her is the dangerous part

phases.name: Smashing Pumpkins
phases.text: Rage. Everything at once: snares, the Harvest Moon, lantern minions and seeds everywhere. Your friends need you as much as you need them.
notes: Free Rindley first, then get to the dome

bosses.feel: A team fight. Your friends hold the sidelines: Sir Rindley charges the Lord and hurls his shield to guard you, Sister Honeydew heals you from across the patch. The Lord keeps trying to pick them off, so you save them, and they save you.
signature: Fight beside Sir Rindley, the Melon Knight, and Sister Honeydew, the Melon Priest
Rindley's Rind Shield circles you and blocks shots
Shoot the vines to free a snared knight
Shelter in the dome Honeydew raises for you

flame.how: Candle fire from inside his carved head

vine.how: Curls as it flies. Often thrown at Sir Rindley

jack.name: Jack-o'-Lantern
jack.how: A grinning lantern that rolls at you and bounces off the walls, then bursts into flame

lines.t: I'll hold the left flank! Watch for my shield!
And I'll keep you whole from the right!
Melons. In MY patch.
Vines, my vines. Hold the knight.
Unhand me, you overgrown squash!
Rise, Harvest Moon!
When my light falls near you, step inside!
The priest goes to sleep first.
Wake her! I'll hold him off!
I will SMASH you all!
Together, now! For the Melon Kingdom!
Light keep us!

death.after: The Pumpkin Lord bursts like a dropped jack-o'-lantern. Sister Honeydew says a blessing over the seeds. Sir Rindley says something less polite.

bosses.name: Mirabeau the Magnificent
bosses.title: The Vanishing Act
bosses.intro: Mirabeau was the greatest illusionist the Velvet Stage ever booked. For his farewell show he promised the impossible: to vanish completely. He stepped into his cabinet, the doors closed, and he was never seen again. He's still performing. He just can't find his way back out of the act.

phases.name: Showtime
phases.text: The curtain rises. Mirabeau sweeps across the stage flicking fans of cards while a spotlight hunts you. Stay in its circle for more than a moment and the empty seats throw a bouquet at you.
notes: The spotlight is slower than you: keep walking and it never catches you
A bouquet lands where you were caught, so step out as soon as the circle turns gold

phases.name: The Double Act
phases.text: His favourite illusion: he becomes your reflection. Mirabeau mirrors you across the middle of the stage, always exactly opposite you, so wherever you lead him is where his scarves come from. And the knife-thrower's act returns: a glint along a line, then a blade.
notes: Move toward the middle and he comes close; stay near a wall and he stays far away
Knife lines glint for a moment before the throw: step off them

phases.name: Find the Lady
phases.text: Mirabeau steps into one of three cabinets and the doors close. The cabinets shuffle across the stage. Keep your eye on his, then stand beside it to open it: find him and he stumbles out, staggered. Open the wrong one and it bursts into cards and doves.
notes: Watch the cabinet, not the cards he throws while they shuffle
Each shuffle is a little faster than the last

phases.name: Encore
phases.text: Encore! The stage remembers your steps. Everywhere you walk lights up, and 1.6s later it erupts. Keep moving into fresh boards, never back the way you came. He throws top hats that burst into doves, and stage rabbits hop after you.
notes: Walk in wide loops: every step you take is a trap for later
A rabbit crouches before it hops: step off its line

phases.name: Trapdoors
phases.text: Scene change. Whole rows of trapdoors drop open across the stage, with one stretch of boards left shut. Sandbags fall from the fly loft, and the spotlight is back, faster.
notes: Each row of trapdoors leaves one safe stretch near you
The spotlight and the trapdoors push you in different directions: pick the trapdoors first

phases.name: Grand Finale
phases.text: Rage. The grand finale. He becomes your reflection again, and the stage still remembers your steps. Lead him without ever walking back over your own path.
notes: Circle the stage: it keeps him moving and keeps you on fresh boards
His rings come from wherever you've led him

bosses.feel: A magic show you're dragged into. A spotlight hunts you, he becomes your reflection, hides in a shuffling cabinet you have to find, and the stage remembers every step you take.
signature: A spotlight that hunts you: the audience throws bouquets if it catches you

Encore: your footsteps erupt behind you

lines.t: The house lights dim. A spotlight finds you.
Ladies and gentlemen! A volunteer from the audience!
For my next trick, I become... you.
Mirabeau's every move begins to mirror yours.
Find the lady!
Mirabeau steps into a cabinet. The doors close.
Watch his cabinet through the shuffle, then stand beside it to open it.
Encore! Encore!
The stage remembers your steps. Each one erupts 1.6s after you leave it.
Scene change!
Trapdoors rattle open across the stage.
Mirabeau sweeps off his hat and bows low.
And now, for my final trick...

death.after: Mirabeau sways, smiles, and with one last flourish of his cape he's gone. This time the cabinet doors swing open on their own, and inside there's nothing but a top hat and a single white dove.

bosses.name: Orrigan
bosses.title: The Thousandth Crane
bosses.intro: Fold a thousand paper cranes and you are granted a wish. Someone folded nine hundred and ninety-nine. The thousandth folded itself, and it grants wishes the way paper cuts: quickly, and deeper than you'd think.

phases.name: A Thousand Cranes
phases.text: Orrigan circles the garden while flocks of paper cranes sweep across it in a V, bobbing as they fly. Paper cuts come straight at you and folded petals open in rings.
notes: A flock comes from one side: slip through the widest gap in the V
The point of the V arrives first, so the wings give you time

phases.name: The Fold
phases.text: The crane folds the garden in half. A crease appears and faint ghosts show where every shot on the far side will land. Then the page folds over and they're all on your side, flying in mirror image.
notes: Watch the ghosts, not the shots: that's where they'll be after the fold
Standing right on the crease is the safest place to be

phases.name: Ink and Brush
phases.text: Ink drops fall across the garden and leave pools that slow you to half speed. Calligraphy strokes slash across the page, and paper frogs hop after you.
notes: Keep your escape routes free of ink: you can't dodge well while you're slowed
Brush strokes show their line first, then slash

phases.name: Paper Storm
phases.text: A storm of paper. Petals spiral out of the crane, flocks cross from both sides, paper darts come straight and fast, and vermilion seals stamp down where you stand.
notes: A seal is a cross: step diagonally out of it
Darts are fast but dead straight. One sidestep is enough

phases.name: The Wish
phases.text: Rage. The crane grants its own wish: everything at once. The garden folds, ink falls, and the flocks never stop.
notes: Before a fold, check the ghosts and the ink: don't get folded into a pool you can't leave

bosses.feel: The page is the battlefield, and the crane can fold it. Flocks of cranes sweep across, ink spills and slows you, and the whole garden folds in half and back again.
signature: Flocks of paper cranes sweeping across the garden
The Fold: the garden folds in half and every shot flips to the other side
Ink pools that slow you down
Calligraphy brush strokes and vermilion seals

crane.name: Paper Crane

lines.t: Nine hundred and ninety-nine sisters.
White flocks rise from the paper trees.
A page has two sides.
A crease runs across the garden.
The Fold: ghosts show where every shot will land when the page folds.
Let the ink run.
Ink begins to fall like rain.
The paper trees shake loose every petal they have.
Wish harder.
You want a wish? Here.
The whole garden begins to fold.

death.after: Orrigan comes apart along its creases, one fold at a time, until it's only a flat square of paper drifting down onto the ink. On it, in a scholar's careful hand: 'I wish for a friend.'

fx: Standing still for 1.5s starts the Still Hour for you: +25% ability cooldown speed until you move

effects.name: Stilled
effects.desc: Caught in the Still Hour: frozen in place.

uniques.name: Polaris Ring
uniques.desc: The star that never moves. Navigators swear by it.
fx: Your aim never drifts: shots ignore Confused and Blind
Abilities mark the nearest enemy with a guiding star: +10% damage taken for 4s

effects.name: Guiding Star
effects.desc: Marked by a star: takes extra damage from everyone.

uniques.name: The Hollow Crown
uniques.desc: A crown that will not let its wearer die. It never says what it takes in return.

effects.name: Checkmate
effects.desc: Nowhere left to go. Takes triple damage from the Usurper's Blade.

uniques.name: Honeydew Blessing
uniques.desc: A pale green charm that smells of summer.
fx: Every 6s, heal yourself and allies within 3.5 tiles for 60 HP

effects.name: Harvest Blessing
effects.desc: Healed by the light of a friendly melon.

uniques.name: The Vanishing Ring
uniques.desc: A plain gold band. Look away and look back, and you'll find it on a different finger.
fx: Above half HP: +12% damage. Below half HP: +12% defense
Encore: your ability repeats once at half strength 1.6s later

effects.name: Encore
effects.desc: The performance repeats itself.

uniques.name: The Thousandth Wish
uniques.desc: A ring with a tiny crane perched on it. Make a wish. Be careful.
fx: Once per dungeon, when an ability would put you at 0 MP, it's free
Abilities fold the space around you: enemy shots within 2 tiles are mirrored away

effects.name: Folded
effects.desc: Folded out of the way: the next hit is halved.

sentry.name: Rusted Sentry
sentry.how: Walks a fixed beat through its tomb. Once it sees you it closes in, slashing a short three-blade fan.

coffin.name: Coffin-Bound
coffin.how: Stands in a burial niche looking like any other coffin. Walk too close and the lid bursts open.

crawler.name: Corpse Crawler
crawler.how: Skulls that crawl out of cracks in the floor in packs and swarm your ankles.

priest.name: Burial Priest
priest.how: Hangs back, casting grave-fire. Every few seconds it raises a fallen corpse, unless the burial seals in its room are broken.

spirit.name: Mourning Spirit
spirit.how: Drifts through walls of grief. Its keening rings slow you and stop you healing.

warden.name: Tomb Warden
warden.how: Heavy armour turns aside a third of every hit. It plods forward and brings its halberd down in a shockwave.

gilded.name: Gilded Skeleton
gilded.how: Rare. A sentry buried in a gold death mask. Tougher, faster, and it always drops treasure.

keeper.name: The Gravekeeper
keeper.how: Guards the Warden's Threshold. Charges, lobs grave-dirt, fires gapped rings; at half health it calls the coffins open and starts raising the dead.
keeper.callMsg: The Gravekeeper rings his lantern. The coffins answer.

crypt.arrive: Dust settles behind you. The mausoleum door is sealed, and the warnings on the walls were scratched by fingernails.
crypt.healMsg: You wash in the font. The candles steady. (Checkpoint)
crypt.shrineMsg: You light the lantern. Your shots burn brighter, and every coffin in the crypt hears it.
crypt.puzzleMsg: The last cursed flame dies. Something grinds open nearby.

id.grammar: Branching catacombs: a spanning tree of small tomb chambers with many dead ends. The main route works inward from the edge of the map toward the central sealed tomb. Some neighbouring tombs share collapsed walls you can shoot through as shortcuts.
id.start: A cracked mausoleum: rows of sealed sarcophagi, cold braziers, scratched warnings and the enormous burial door you came to open, which won't budge. Dust drifts in the light from the portal.
id.landmark: Burial halls lined with coffins in wall niches. The Warden's Threshold is the central sealed tomb, ringed with coffins that never stop rattling.
id.feature: The crypt awakens as you go deeper. Coffins knock, sarcophagus lids slide open, and dormant dead start getting up on their own.
id.ante: The Warden's Threshold: a pillared tomb with burial niches on both sides and the sealed door of Gravewarden Mortis at its head.
traps: The Coffin-Bound stand in niches looking like furniture and burst out when you pass.
Cracked ossuary floors give way a moment after you step on them, then settle again.
Green-fire braziers in embalming halls flare in a burst when you are near.
Bony hands lurking in the floor grab your ankles and hold you still.
Burial halls slam their doorways shut behind you until every enemy inside is dead.
secrets: A burial wall with a hairline crack and cobwebs in the corner breaks if you shoot it.
One sarcophagus in a burial hall has its lid slightly ajar. Search it.
A sealed vault opens only once you snuff the three cursed flames burning elsewhere in the crypt.
An old crypt keeper dozes in a dead-end tomb. Wake him for a gift and a warning.
Rubble-choked walls between neighbouring tombs can be shot through.

lore: The masons who sealed this crypt carved a warning on the door. Someone scratched it out.
A ledger of the dead. The last hundred names are written in the same hand, and the ink is still wet.
'He walks the rounds at midnight. If you hear the bell, you are already late.'
A broken lantern, the same make as the Warden's. Its owner didn't make it past this room.
mutations: Bell Ringers appear in every hall
Gilded Skeletons are far more common, and so is treasure

rat.name: Mutant Rat
rat.how: Comes in packs, fast and fragile, flanking from the sides while you deal with something bigger.

slime.name: Sewer Slime
slime.how: Oozes after you leaving a poisoned trail, and splits into two slimelets when it dies.

slimelet.name: Slimelet
slimelet.how: What's left of a slime. Quick and weak.

toad.name: Bloat Toad
toad.how: Hops toward you, then spits a bile glob that lands where you were standing.

leech.name: Pipe Leech
leech.how: Wriggles out of the wall pipes while you're near. Its bite stops you healing.

scav.name: Diseased Scavenger
scav.how: Keeps its distance, flinging rusty scrap two at a time and throwing a weighted net that pins you in place.

crawdad.name: Armoured Crawdad
crawdad.how: A huge crustacean. Its shell turns away half of every hit; it clamps down with a slam, and dives into the channels to close the gap.

lurker.name: Channel Lurker
lurker.how: Swims under the sludge where nothing can hit it, surfacing beside you to spit, then diving again.

goldrat.name: Golden Rat
goldrat.how: Rare: the rat king's heir. It runs from you, and drops a fortune if you catch it.

dredger.name: The Dredger
dredger.how: A crab the size of a cart, crusted with a century of rubbish. Slams shockwaves, sprays sludge in fans and calls leeches from the pipes; below half health it floods the floor in rings.
dredger.callMsg: The Dredger shrieks. Rats pour out of the walls.

sewers.arrive: You climb down the maintenance ladder. Water drips somewhere ahead, and something big moves under the sludge.
sewers.healMsg: Clean water from the old maintenance tap. You drink and rinse the filth off. (Checkpoint)
sewers.shrineMsg: You leave a bottle cap at the rat idol. Your shots sting harder, and the pack has smelled you.

id.grammar: A looping drainage network. Round chambers sit on a loose lattice and most neighbours connect, so routes keep reconnecting. Every tunnel carries a sludge channel down its middle with a walkway either side, and the channels are how you find your way.
id.start: A damp maintenance access chamber: the ladder down, dripping pipes, rusted grates, a lamp, and a wastewater channel crossing the floor with something moving under it.
id.landmark: Reservoirs whose water level rises and falls, and the Throne Pipe: a grated sluice chamber with the Gutterlord's sealed door.
id.feature: The water moves. Reservoir rooms flood and drain on a cycle. Low water opens passages and exposes what was hiding in them; high water drowns the floor in toxic sludge and lets the lurkers hunt.
id.ante: The Throne Pipe: a grated sluice room where the channels all drain toward the Gutterlord's door.
traps: Burst wall pipes spray sludge across the tunnel in pressure pulses.
The sludge burns and stops you healing; walkways keep you out of it.
Rusted grate bridges over the channels drop away after you cross.
Filtration rooms vent scalding steam in rows.
Toxic barrels explode when shot: dangerous to you, deadlier to whatever is standing next to them.
secrets: A draft blows from one grated wall. Walk into it.
A tunnel that only drains at low water leads to a scavenger cache.
Turn the valves in the order painted on the maintenance sign to open the sluice cache.
A cracked wall in a dead end hides the nest where the golden rats breed.

lore: A sewerman's tally on the wall: three hundred and twelve rats. The last mark is a crown.
'Don't drink from the channel. Don't sleep near the drains. Don't follow the music.'
A smuggler's map of the tunnels. Every route ends at the same grate, circled twice.
Somebody built a little throne out of bottle caps and left it here, facing the dark.
mutations: The water is high and every enemy moves faster
Rat Pipers lead swarms into every hall
Golden Rat Kings are common, and so is gold

shambler.name: Rootbound Shambler
shambler.how: Lurches after you trailing roots; up close it plants itself and the ground grabs your feet.

snapjaw.name: Snapjaw Bloom
snapjaw.how: Looks like any other flower until you're close. Then it opens and spits petal fans. It also wakes when its neighbours are hurt.

blightwisp.name: Blighted Wisp
blightwisp.how: A corrupted woodland spirit. It mends wounded plants and hurls stinging bubbles.

sporecap.name: Sporecap
sporecap.how: Waddles about puffing rings of spores that stop you healing. Bursts into a last cloud when it dies.

vine.name: Strangler Vine
vine.how: Grows from the wall and lashes a line of thorns at you. Each hit can root you. Wakes when a neighbour is hurt.

barkback.name: Barkback
barkback.how: A beast of bark that sleeps as a stump. Bark armour turns aside a third of every hit; its slam throws splinters.

moontoad.name: Moon Toad
moontoad.how: Rare: a pale toad that glows like the moon. It hops away from you, and drops treasure when caught.

rootmother.name: Old Rootmother
rootmother.how: Mother Mire's oldest servant, a hag grown into a tree. Lobs spore pods, fires gapped petal rings and drags roots across the floor; below half health she calls the shamblers and the bog itself rises in bubbling rings.
rootmother.callMsg: The Rootmother groans. The ground splits and shamblers climb out.

mire.arrive: You come out beneath roots as thick as houses. Fireflies drift in the dark, and the trees seem to lean in to look at you.
mire.healMsg: You drink from the spring. It tastes of moss and moonlight. (Checkpoint)
mire.shrineMsg: You touch the woodland shrine. Green fire runs up your arms, and every plant in the hollow turns toward you.

id.grammar: Organic: irregular clearings grown from overlapping circles, scattered without a grid and joined by winding, uneven paths. The links form a minimum spanning tree with a few extra loops, so routes branch around the giant trees and sometimes meet again.
id.start: A small clearing beneath enormous twisted roots, with fireflies drifting in the dark and a broken woodland shrine.
id.landmark: Giant trees and glowing toadstools that you have to walk around, and Mother's Doorstep: the witch's hut door at the edge of a dark pond.
id.feature: The forest is alive. Flowers open as you pass, roots shift underfoot, plants sleep until a neighbour is hurt, and dormant stumps get up.
id.ante: Mother's Doorstep: a clearing of hexcap rings and bubbling pools before the witch's door.
traps: Root-tangled ground grabs and holds you.
Puffballs by the giant mushrooms burst into clouds that stop you healing.
Vines in the walls lash thorns across the path.
Brambles hurt every step you take through them.
Snapjaw Blooms pose as flowers and open fire when you come close.
secrets: One giant tree is hollow. A gap between its roots lets you walk inside.
A trail of fireflies leads to a wall of leaves that hides the firefly shrine.
Stand in the middle of a ring of pale mushrooms and wait. Something is given to those who are patient.
An abandoned cabin with the herbalist's notes and her last remedies.

lore: A recipe card, splashed with something green: 'One adventurer, well rinsed.'
The lanterns here were lit to guide travellers in. Nobody ever lit one to guide them out.
'She was a midwife once. The whole village loved her. Then the village sank.'
A child's boot in the reeds, and a trail of tiny frog prints leading away from it.
mutations: You can see less of the marsh around you
Bog flies and toads swarm in every clearing
Moon Toads are common, and so is treasure

construct.name: Molten Construct
construct.how: Slow and heavy, leaving burning slag where it walks. Every so often it glows white-hot and bursts in a ring of fire.

smith.name: Ash-Smith
smith.how: A soot-black smith who closes in swinging. Near an anvil it works faster and its hammer throws sparks.

imp.name: Furnace Imp
imp.how: Swoops in to spit fire and darts back out of reach.

armour.name: Animated Armour
armour.how: Stands on its rack with the others until you walk past. Armour turns aside 40% of every hit.

slagbug.name: Slag Crawler
slagbug.how: Swarms out of the slag heaps, each one leaving a burning streak behind it.

sentry.name: Mechanical Sentry
sentry.how: A tripod turret left on guard. It sweeps a spiral of sparks and fires aimed bursts.

goldgolem.name: Gold Golem
goldgolem.how: Rare: a construct poured from the treasury's gold. Slow, tough, and worth a fortune.

engine.name: The Foreman Engine
engine.how: A walking boiler that ran the city's shifts. It sweeps triple spirals, lobs slag and vents itself white-hot; at half health it calls the imps and starts leaving fire everywhere it steps.
engine.callMsg: The Foreman Engine's whistle shrieks. The furnaces empty.

forge.arrive: You come through the burned city gate. The cobbles are still warm. Somewhere ahead, the great forge is still burning.
forge.healMsg: You plunge your arms into the quenching trough. The steam clears your head. (Checkpoint)
forge.shrineMsg: You feed the experimental forge. Your shots come out white-hot, and every furnace in the city roars.

id.grammar: A ruined city on a grid. Wide streets meet in plazas, and buildings fill the blocks between them, each opening onto a street through its own door. Collapsed segments block some streets and force detours, and lava channels run down the middle of others. The main route crosses the city plaza by plaza to the great foundry.
id.start: The burned city gate: a gatehouse with a jammed portcullis, blackened masonry, cooling metal, a fallen gear from the gate machinery, and the glow of the great forge on the skyline.
id.landmark: Foundries with conveyor floors, lava pools and swinging hammers, and the Great Foundry door behind its lava moat.
id.feature: It is a ruined city, not a cave. You walk streets, enter buildings through their doors, take detours round collapsed blocks and cross lava channels.
id.ante: The Great Foundry: a lava moat crossed by one bridge, braziers, and the Great Forge before Forgemaster Cinder's door.
traps: Lava runs down the middle of some streets and through foundry floors. It burns badly.
Furnace mouths flare in bursts that blast out fire.
Trip-hammers in the foundries sweep the floor in a slow circle.
Foundry belts carry you along whether you like it or not.
Steam squares vent from the cobbles in rows.
Grated walkways over the lava drop away after you step on them.
secrets: A bricked-up doorway with soot around the frame. Shoot through it.
Its lock answers to the Foreman Engine's key.
Pump the three bellows in turn while the furnace is hot.
Deep in the city, the founding smith's last blade lies on its anvil, still warm.

lore: A quota board: 'Swords: 400. Shields: 400. Smiths: replace as needed.'
An apprentice's first hammer, never used. Someone kept it polished anyway.
'The fires went out once, and he relit them with the first thing to hand.'
The ingots in this stack are stamped with names instead of weights.
mutations: The forge is running hot and every enemy moves faster
Your vision is cut short by the smoke
Gold Golems are common, and so is treasure

lunarwisp.name: Lunar Wisp
lunarwisp.how: A mote of moonlight. Out of the moonbeams you can barely touch it; in them it bursts at a touch.

moonmoth.name: Moon Moth
moonmoth.how: Flutters in circles around you, shedding dust that slows you.

wolf.name: Silverfang
wolf.how: A silver-furred predator that stalks in the shadows and lunges along a straight line.

bloom.name: Moonbloom
bloom.how: An enchanted flower rooted in place. Its petals fire as a fan, and a stray moonbeam is reflected back at you from its face.

stag.name: Spectral Stag
stag.how: A deer of starlight that charges, leaving a trail of shadow that drags at your feet. Only solid in moonlight.

guardian.name: Moonbound Guardian
guardian.how: A stone knight of the old sanctuary. Its crescent glaive throws arcs; stone turns aside a third of every hit.

shade.name: Moving Shadow
shade.how: A shadow cast by nothing. It slides across the grass toward you and slows whatever it touches.

silvermoth.name: Silver Moth
silvermoth.how: Rare: a moth with wings of beaten silver. It flees the light, and drops treasure when caught.

warden.name: The Silk Warden
warden.how: A great moth-knight. It circles, sheds rings of moon-scales and lunges; at half health it calls the moths and a moonbeam follows it everywhere, so it can only be hurt while lit.
warden.callMsg: The Silk Warden's wings blaze. Moths pour out of the dark.

glade.arrive: You step out under a moon that never sets. The clearing is silver and quiet, and the pools hold more stars than the sky.
glade.healMsg: You drink from the moon well. The light settles in you. (Checkpoint)
glade.shrineMsg: You kneel at the lunar shrine. Your shots shine like moonlight, and the guardians of the glade have noticed you.

id.grammar: Open and graceful: a few large clearings, crescents and ponds joined by long curving trails. Every reflecting pool has a path that loops all the way round it, and side groves branch off the main trails.
id.start: A tranquil moonlit clearing: silver ferns, pale stone arches, and a shallow pool full of reflected stars.
id.landmark: Reflecting pools with their circular walks, and the pale stone arches of the ruined sanctuaries.
id.feature: Moonlight is a mechanic. Pools of moonlight drift slowly across the glade. Spirits of the glade can only be hurt while they are lit. Some paths only appear when a moonbeam crosses a particular stone.
id.ante: The Moonlit Lawn: a crescent of standing stones under the brightest light in the glade, before the Matriarch's moon-gate.
traps: Concentrated moonlight falls in marked circles.
Patches of shadow creep across the floor and drag at your feet.
Moonblooms turn to face you and fire.
Shots that cross a reflecting pool are mirrored back the other way.
The pools glow brighter and brighter, then flare and burn anyone standing in them.
secrets: When a drifting moonbeam crosses the moonstone, the path beside it opens. Wait for the light.
A curtain of silver ferns hides a fairy grove. Walk into it.
Locked behind the Silk Warden's seal.
A well in a quiet corner restores you.

lore: Every moth here flies toward the same pale light in the north.
A poacher's net, full of torn silver wings. The poacher is nowhere to be seen.
'Don't bring a lantern. She hates any light but hers.'
The moonflowers close as you pass, and open again behind you.
mutations: The glade is darker than usual
Caterpillars and moths fill every clearing
Silver Moths are common, and so is treasure

knight.name: Icebound Knight
knight.how: Stands sealed in a block of ice until you come close. Its rimed armour turns aside a third of every hit; when it falls it shatters into flying shards.

spirit.name: Frost Spirit
spirit.how: Hangs back and seals its allies in ice so your shots can't touch them until you break the ice off.

mite.name: Crystal Mite
mite.how: Glassy insects that swarm across the ice, skittering faster than you can slide.

bear.name: Rime Bear
bear.how: Charges across the ice in straight lines, freezing the floor behind it into a slick that slows you.

underice.name: The Thing Under the Ice
underice.how: Swims beneath the frozen lake where nothing can hit it, then smashes up through the ice beside you.

crystal.name: Refracting Crystal
crystal.how: A living crystal. Your shots bounce off it, except just after it fires. Enemy shots that pass through it split into fans.

diamond.name: Diamond Golem
diamond.how: Rare: a crystal as clear as water and worth a kingdom. Reflects your shots except right after it fires.

colossus.name: The Glacier Warden
colossus.how: An ice giant crowned in spires. It slams the ice, sprays spirals of icicles and seals itself in ice until you break it out; at half health it calls the mites and lobs frost bombs.
colossus.callMsg: The Glacier Warden roars. The walls crack and crystal mites pour out.

unmelting.arrive: Your breath freezes as you step through. Explorers stand all around the cavern, frozen in the middle of a stride, and none of them have aged a day.
unmelting.healMsg: A hot spring, impossibly, here. You thaw out. (Checkpoint)
unmelting.shrineMsg: You feed the last flame. Your shots burn hot enough to melt the unmelting, and the ice itself turns to look at you.

id.grammar: Glacial networks: jagged caverns grown by cellular automata, joined by narrow ice passages. Walls of breakable ice separate some routes, and ice bridges cross chasms that drop into the dark.
id.start: A frost-covered cavern: explorers frozen mid-stride all around, and at its centre a gigantic crystal of perfectly clear ice with something dark inside.
id.landmark: Frozen lakes of slick black ice, and the gigantic clear crystal.
id.feature: Ice is a system, not a texture. Black ice makes you slide and keep your momentum. Ice walls break when shot. Crystals reflect your shots and split enemy shots into fans. Things are preserved in the ice, and some of them wake up.
id.ante: The Unmelting Door: a hall of frost spires and frozen banners where the cold is strongest.
traps: Black ice keeps your momentum: you slide, and must steer early.
Icicles drop from the ceiling where shadows mark the floor.
Thin ice on the lakes cracks and gives way after you step on it.
Mist corridors breathe out a freezing fog that slows you, row by row.
Drifts erupt in bursts of hail.
Ice bridges over the chasms crack and fall after you cross.
secrets: Some walls are only ice. Shoot them.
A chest frozen in a block of ice. Break it free.
A creature preserved in the ice for a thousand years. Shatter its prison, if you dare, for what it was guarding.
Their camp, their journal, and the supplies they never got to use.

lore: The adventurer in the ice is still holding a torch. It's still lit.
'Walk softly. The ice remembers footsteps.'
A journal: 'Day 9. The walls are closer than yesterday.'
Somebody carved a sun into the ice wall, over and over, until their tools broke.
mutations: Blowing snow cuts your vision short
Diamond Golems are common, and so is treasure

parasite.name: Meteor Parasite
parasite.how: Ticks of black glass that pour out of the meteor fragments. Their bite stops you healing.

shardback.name: Shardback
shardback.how: A beast with crystal growing out of its back. It charges, and when it dies the crystals break off and keep coming.

shardling.name: Shardling
shardling.how: A broken-off crystal that skitters after you.

debris.name: Debris Construct
debris.how: Rocks orbiting a pulsing core. It drifts close and pulls you in with bursts of gravity, then fires the rocks.

starspawn.name: Starspawn
starspawn.how: An alien bag of eyes that hangs back firing shots that curve in from the sides.

burrower.name: Rock Burrower
burrower.how: A blind predator that tunnels under the crater floor, surfacing beside you in a burst of rock.

prism.name: Prism Wanderer
prism.how: Rare: a living prism of starlight. It flees, and leaves a fortune of starmetal behind.

champion.name: The Fallen Champion
champion.how: The knight who led the expedition to claim the star, crystal growing through his armour. He throws blade fans, pulls you in with gravity and calls down the sky; at half health the parasites swarm out of him.
champion.callMsg: The Fallen Champion's armour cracks open. Parasites boil out.

crater.arrive: You come over the crater rim. Below, the ground falls away in broken rings toward a glow at the bottom, and the rocks hum.
crater.healMsg: A spring that the impact didn't poison. You drink and wash the glass dust off. (Checkpoint)
crater.shrineMsg: You touch the fallen star's shrine. Starlight runs through your shots, and something at the bottom of the crater turns toward you.

id.grammar: Radial: rooms sit on three concentric broken rings around the impact core, with arcing paths along each ring and fissures running inward between them. The way in spirals down from the rim to the crater's heart.
id.start: The crater rim: fractured rock looking down into the impact, meteor fragments scattered about, and the glow of the impact scar at the bottom.
id.landmark: The impact core at the dead centre of the map, and the hollow meteor fragment.
id.feature: The ground tells you how close you are. Toward the centre the rock turns to starglass, the crystals thicken, gravity pulls harder and shockwaves roll out from the core.
id.ante: The Heart of the Crater: a ring of starglass around the fallen star's core, where Astraeus waits.
traps: Pieces of the star still fall. Watch for the shadows.
Cracks in the inner ring give way under your feet.
Crystal clusters burst in rings of shards.
Pockets of warped gravity drag you toward their centre.
Every few seconds a shockwave rolls out from the core. Get behind rock before it reaches you.
secrets: Some meteor fragments are shells. Shoot them open.
A pulsing artifact half-buried behind a wall of glass.
Fissures in the wall that you can shoot through.
A meteor the size of a house. Walk into the crack in its side.

lore: A shield split clean in half. The edges are melted glass.
'It fell for three nights. On the fourth, it stood up.'
The knights who came to claim the star built a camp here. They never broke it down.
Every compass in this crater points straight down.
mutations: Prism Wanderers are common, and so is treasure

sunaco.name: Sun Acolyte
sunaco.how: Fights alongside a Moon Acolyte. It can only be hurt while the sun is up, and its rays cross its partner's.

moonaco.name: Moon Acolyte
moonaco.how: Fights alongside a Sun Acolyte. It can only be hurt while the moons are up, and its rings fill the gaps in its partner's fire.

priest.name: Eclipse Priest
priest.how: Shields whichever partner is vulnerable at the moment, and fires a black disc that splits in two.

sunsentry.name: Sun Sentry
sunsentry.how: A celestial sentry that fires only on the even beats of the temple's rhythm.

moonsentry.name: Moon Sentry
moonsentry.how: A celestial sentry that fires only on the odd beats, so the two of them never fire at once.

spirit.name: Moonbound Spirit
spirit.how: Drifts at the edges of the fight, laying down slow rings that fill in whatever gaps the others leave.

dawn.name: Dawn Guardian
dawn.how: One of a pair: the sun-disc guardian. Only hurt while the sun is up; throws sun-discs that cross the Dusk Guardian's blades.

dusk.name: Dusk Guardian
dusk.how: One of a pair: the moon-blade guardian. Only hurt while the moons are up.

idol.name: Eclipse Idol
idol.how: Rare: a gilded idol with a black sun for a face. It hurts only while day and night are changing over.

sunwarden.name: The Sun Warden
sunwarden.how: Warden of the sun wing. It can only be hurt by day. It fires sweeping disc fans and calls Sun Acolytes; at half health it starts throwing rings.
sunwarden.callMsg: The Sun Warden raises its halo. Acolytes answer.

moonwarden.name: The Moon Warden
moonwarden.how: Warden of the moon wing. It can only be hurt by night. It fires spirals and calls Moon Acolytes; at half health it starts dashing.
moonwarden.callMsg: The Moon Warden's crescent darkens. Acolytes answer.

temple.arrive: You step into a courtyard split down the middle: gold on one side, silver on the other, and two great statues watching you.
temple.healMsg: You drink from the twin basin. One half of the water is warm, the other cold. (Checkpoint)
temple.shrineMsg: You touch the shrine of the two faces. Your shots carry both lights, and both wings know you're here.

id.grammar: Two interconnected wings, built as mirror images either side of a central axis: the sun wing on the left, the moon wing on the right. The wings share a courtyard and a central hall, and you can explore them in either order. Each ends at a warden, and the central sanctuary opens only when both wardens are dead.
id.start: A symmetrical courtyard with two enormous statues, one pale and one dark, and the floor split between gold and silver mosaic.
id.landmark: The twin statues, rotating star charts, and the central sanctuary on the axis between the wings.
id.feature: Duality. Day and night trade places on a fixed rhythm. Sun creatures can only be hurt by day and moon creatures by night, so every pair covers for its partner. Sentries fire on alternating beats, puzzles need two keys, and both wings have to fall.
id.ante: The Central Sanctuary: the eclipse altar between the wings, where the Eclipse Twins wait.
traps: Beams sweep the eclipse halls, the sun beam by day and the moon beam by night.
Pools of total darkness where you can see almost nothing.
Two plates in mirrored rooms must both be pressed in a few seconds of each other.
The great orrery's arms sweep the inner rite.
Sun and moon sentries fire on alternate beats. Move between them.
secrets: Each wing has a lever, one sun and one moon. Set both to open the hidden sanctuary on the central axis.
Twin plates, one in each wing. Press one, then run to the other before its light fades.
Behind a gate that opens to a warden's key.

lore: Every mural shows the same two figures. In the oldest ones, they're holding hands.
'One rules the day. One rules the night. Never stand in both at once.'
A scribe's tablet, half sun-bleached and half moon-dark.
The offering bowls are full of coins from a kingdom that no longer exists.
mutations: The temple is plunged into shadow
Priests summon more help in every hall
Gilded Idols are common, and so is treasure

crawler.name: Rift Crawler
crawler.how: Swarms toward you, blinking a few steps forward through space when it loses sight of you.

stalker.name: Phase Stalker
stalker.how: Shifts out of phase, invisible and untouchable, then reappears beside you to slash.

sentry.name: Void Sentry
sentry.how: A floating eye. Every shot it fires repeats a second later from the same spot. Dodge twice.

apparition.name: Unstable Apparition
apparition.how: Blinks around you leaving afterimages, and fires a ring from wherever it lands.

fragment.name: Fragmented Entity
fragment.how: A body that doesn't hold together. Hit it and it comes apart into pieces that keep attacking.

echo.name: Echo
echo.how: Attacks from where it is and from where it has just been. Its afterimages fire too.

starchild.name: Lost Starchild
starchild.how: Rare: a child-shaped hole full of stars. It flees through space, and leaves a fortune behind.

herald.name: The Herald of Nothing
herald.how: It blinks around its platform, fires rings that come back a second later, and opens tears that spill crawlers. At half health its afterimages start shooting too.
herald.callMsg: The Herald tears the air open. Crawlers spill through.

rift.arrive: The cavern is split down the middle by a tear in the world. Stone floats around it. Your footsteps sound a moment before you take them.
rift.healMsg: The pool here is still, in a way nothing else in the rift is. (Checkpoint)
rift.shrineMsg: You reach into the altar of absence. Your shots arrive a little before you fire them, and everything in the rift turns its head.

id.grammar: Non-linear: platforms float in the void, and most of them connect through paired rifts rather than corridors. A rift can join two places that are nowhere near each other. Short stone bridges link a few neighbours, and the antechamber is reached by the only bridge that holds still.
id.start: A cavern split by a luminous tear in reality, with broken stone fragments floating around it.
id.landmark: The great tear, and the void itself: you can see platforms you can't reach, hanging in the dark.
id.feature: Space is unstable but fair. Rifts carry you between distant platforms and every one shows where it leads. Enemies blink, phase out and echo their own attacks.
id.ante: The Edge of Everything: a last stable platform where the floor simply ends in stars.
traps: Tears in the air flare and spill shards.
Fields of shimmering floor throw you somewhere else on the platform.
Parts of a platform drop out into the void after you step on them, and come back later.
Void sentries' shots repeat a second later.
Some rifts flicker on and off. Wait for them to open.
secrets: One of the dangerous-looking fractures isn't a hazard at all. Step into it.
A vault on a platform of its own, behind the Herald's lock.
An unstable rift leads somewhere rare, but only while it holds open.

lore: The chains here weren't made to keep something in. They were made to keep something out.
'If it looks at you, don't look back.'
A map of this place, drawn three times. Each one is different.
Your footsteps echo a moment before you take them.
mutations: Lost Starchildren are common, and so is treasure

clergy.name: Drowned Clergy
clergy.how: Keeps its distance, sending out slow expanding rings of water that drag at your legs.

skeleton.name: Waterlogged Skeleton
skeleton.how: Lies under the floodwater until you wade past, then rises dripping and attacks.

chorister.name: Spectral Chorister
chorister.how: Circles its choirmaster in formation, all of them singing. Kill the choirmaster and the choir breaks apart.

master.name: Choirmaster
master.how: Conducts the spectral choir. While it lives the choir circles it; every few bars they all sing together, a ring of hymns.

parasite.name: Aquatic Parasite
parasite.how: Swims in schools through the flooded passages and bites anything that wades in.

sentinel.name: Barnacle Sentinel
sentinel.how: A saint's statue crusted with barnacles. Its shell turns away half of every hit; it fires pearls in a spread.

pearlknight.name: Pearl Knight
pearlknight.how: Rare: a drowned knight clad in pearl. It always drops treasure.

organist.name: The Drowned Organist
organist.how: Grown into his organ's pipes. He plays rings of notes and slow walls of water, and calls the drowned up out of the floor; at half health the music becomes a spiral.
organist.callMsg: The organ thunders. The drowned climb out of the water.

chapel.arrive: Water laps around your ankles. Candles float on it, still lit, drifting past pews that rot in rows toward a broken window.
chapel.healMsg: You drink from the font, the one place the sea hasn't reached. (Checkpoint)
chapel.shrineMsg: You touch the pearl shrine. Your shots ring like bells, and every drowned thing in the chapel lifts its head.
chapel.doorMsg: The altar rail, beyond which waits

id.grammar: Interconnected chapel buildings. Every pair of linked halls has two routes: a narrow dry walkway along the upper wall, and a broad flooded passage through the lower crypts where the water slows you and things swim. The halls join up into loops through both.
id.start: A partly flooded chapel porch: sunken pews, floating candles, and the broken stained-glass window ahead.
id.landmark: The broken rose window, still throwing coloured light, and the organ loft.
id.feature: Water is architecture. The dry routes are narrow and exposed; the flooded routes are wide but slow and full of things. The tide rises and falls in the nave, electrified pools crackle, and draining the right chamber changes what you can reach.
id.ante: The Altar Rail: candles floating in a ring around the drowned altar, before the Cantor's door.
traps: The nave floods to waist height on a cycle, then drains.
Rotten floorboards over the crypts give way after you step on them.
Drains in the flooded crypts pull you toward them.
The bell tower drops its bells where their shadows fall.
Water jets out of the old pipes.
Pools that crackle with current on a rhythm.
secrets: One of the confessionals is a door. Walk into it.
Pull the sexton's lever to drain a flooded vault and uncover the submerged shrine.
Locked, and the Organist keeps the key.
A walled-up burial vault behind barnacled stone. Shoot it open.

lore: The hymn books are swollen with water, but they still fall open to the same page.
'Sing, and the water stays low. Stop, and it rises.'
A parish roll. Every name is marked 'still singing'.
You can hear the organ through the walls. It's playing your footsteps.
mutations: Deacons fill every hall with help
Pearl Knights are common, and so is treasure

knight.name: Oathbound Knight
knight.how: Sworn to the grove. It holds its post beside a sacred stone, and if you strike the stone, it and every other guardian comes for you angrier.

barkguard.name: Barkguard
barkguard.how: A living tree-trunk with a fungus shield. Slow, heavy, and it roots you with a stamp of its feet.

hart.name: Enchanted Hart
hart.how: Charges in straight lines with its branch-antlers lowered.

sentinel.name: Spectral Sentinel
sentinel.how: A ghost-archer bound to the stones. Holds still and looses aimed volleys; it can see you a long way off.

spirit.name: Grove Spirit
spirit.how: A protective spirit that drifts among the guardians mending their wounds.

blight.name: Blight Crawler
blight.how: The only thing in the grove that wants the sacred trees dead. It goes for the sapling, not for you.

goldstag.name: Golden Stag
goldstag.how: Rare: a stag with a coat of beaten gold. It runs, and it leaves treasure behind.

druid.name: The Elder Druid
druid.how: Keeper of the oath. Calls roots across the floor, looses leaf fans and seed storms, and shields itself with the grove; at half health the guardians answer its horn.
druid.callMsg: The Elder Druid sounds its horn. The oath answers.

grove.arrive: You enter a ring of standing stones, each carved with promises in a language nobody speaks any more. Beyond them is the largest tree you have ever seen.
grove.healMsg: You drink from the clear spring at the foot of the stones. (Checkpoint)
grove.shrineMsg: You make an offering at the oath shrine. The grove accepts you, for now: your shots are blessed.
grove.doorMsg: The heart of the grove, where

id.grammar: A pilgrimage around a sacred landmark. The Heart Oak stands at the centre of the map, ringed by a circular pilgrim's way. Clearings branch off the ring like spokes, with more groves further out. You walk the ring to reach the far side, where the oak's roots open onto the elder's glade.
id.start: A ceremonial ring of standing stones engraved with forgotten promises, and the massive ancient oak beyond them.
id.landmark: The Heart Oak: you can see it from the pilgrim's way all the way round.
id.feature: The grove is sacred and defensive, not corrupted. Its guardians hold posts beside sacred stones and trees. Strike one and the grove retaliates: guardians enrage, roots grab at you, and the doors seal. Protecting things is rewarded.
id.ante: The Heart Oak's Roots: a cave of roots beneath the great tree, where Elderbark keeps the oath.
traps: Roots across the path grab and hold you.
Guardians standing in a rune circle can't be harmed. Draw them out of it.
Statues watch the pilgrim's way and loose arrows at anyone who has broken the oath.
Damage a sacred stone or tree and the clearing seals you in with its angry guardians.
secrets: Blight crawlers come for a sacred sapling. Protect it until the trial ends and the grove rewards you.
A hidden stone behind a curtain of ribbons, its oath still legible.
An ancient guardian's resting place, walled up. Shoot the stone.

lore: An axe buried in a stump. The bark has grown over the handle.
'Swear to the grove, and the grove keeps you. Forever.'
The woodcutters left a list of trees they'd cut. Every one of them is standing.
Somebody carved their name into a tree here. The tree has carved it back, larger.
mutations: Golden Stags are common, and so is treasure

harpy.name: Storm Harpy
harpy.how: Swoops in from over the drop, rakes you with a feather volley, and wheels away out of reach.

elemental.name: Lightning Elemental
elemental.how: Always comes in pairs. A bolt of lightning arcs between them; never walk through it.

sentry.name: Mountain Sentry
sentry.how: A crossbowman on the walls and in the watchtowers. It holds its post and fires bolts in strings.

thunderbird.name: Thunderbird
thunderbird.how: A great dark bird that dives along straight lines and drops lightning where it has flown.

knight.name: Storm Knight
knight.how: Armoured in steel that turns aside a third of every hit. Its forked spear brings down a ring of lightning.

goldroc.name: Gold-Feathered Roc
goldroc.how: Rare: a roc chick with golden feathers. It flees, and drops treasure when caught.

chief.name: The Storm Chief
chief.how: A harpy-queen crowned with lightning rods. She swoops, fans feathers, and calls lightning down in rings; at half health her elementals arrive in pairs.
chief.callMsg: The Storm Chief shrieks. Lightning answers, in pairs.

peaks.arrive: Wind tears at you the moment you step through. The path clings to the cliff face, and far above, through the cloud, there is a fortress.
peaks.healMsg: A shepherd's shelter, out of the wind. You catch your breath. (Checkpoint)
peaks.shrineMsg: You touch the storm shrine. Lightning runs down your arm into your shots, and the storm takes notice of you.

id.grammar: A winding ascent. Narrow ledges are stacked up the cliff from the pass at the bottom to the fortress at the top, joined at alternating ends by stairs cut into the rock, so the route switches back and forth as it climbs. Below every ledge the cliff drops away into cloud. Watchtowers and caves branch off the ledges, and the top ledge is the fortress.
id.start: A windswept mountain pass: torn banners, a dead watchtower, and the fortress far above through the clouds.
id.landmark: The fortress on the summit, which you can see from the pass and get closer to with every switchback.
id.feature: Height. You can always see the drop below you, the ledge you just climbed and the cliff face rising above. Wind pushes you toward the edge, and lightning finds the highest metal.
id.ante: The Summit Hall: the fortress's last yard under the storm, where Tempest Roc nests.
traps: On the ridges lightning falls where it is marked, and especially near the rods.
Gusts sweep the ledges toward the drop. You'll see them coming in the streaks.
Rope bridges between ledges snap after you cross.
Rockfall slopes shed boulders from the cliffs above.
Elementals arc lightning between each other. The bolt hurts.
Charged stone sparks in rows when the storm builds.
secrets: One lightning rod stands beside a seam in the cliff. Stand on the copper plate when the lightning comes and the rock splits.
A dark crack in the cliff face that you can walk into.
A watchtower nobody manned again, and its last log.
Locked away by the Storm Chief.

lore: A rope tied to an iron spike. It's been cut, neatly, from above.
'When the feathers fall upward, climb down.'
The shepherds here pray to the storm. The storm answers.
A climber's log: 'Summit tomorrow.' The pages after that are blank.
mutations: Lightning hits the ledges more often
Gold-Feathered Rocs are common, and so is treasure

cultist.name: Ember Cultist
cultist.how: Keeps its distance and lobs clay firebombs that leave the floor burning where they land.

phoenixling.name: Phoenixling
phoenixling.how: Swoops in fast. When it dies it leaves an ember, and if you don't stamp the ember out it is reborn from it.

eel.name: Magma Eel
eel.how: Lives in the lava. It swims unseen, surfaces near the bank to spit molten globs, and dives again.

brute.name: Obsidian Brute
brute.how: Its black-glass hide shrugs off most of every shot until it slams the floor. Then the magma shows in its cracks and it can be hurt.

ashpriest.name: Ash Priest
ashpriest.how: Hangs back by the ash heaps and calls emberlings up out of them, two at a time.

emberling.name: Emberling
emberling.how: A hopping spark. It comes straight at you and bursts into a ring of cinders when it dies.

goldchick.name: Golden Phoenix Chick
goldchick.how: Rare: a phoenix chick with golden feathers. It flees, and drops treasure when caught.

cinderlord.name: The Cinder Lord
cinderlord.how: Keeper of the pyre. He lobs magma in rings and drives a line of fire at you; at half health the phoenixlings come down from the summit to fight for him.
cinderlord.callMsg: The Cinder Lord raises his staff. Phoenixlings dive from the summit.

pyre.arrive: Heat hits you like a wall. Below the ledge a river of magma slides past, and across it, to the east, the mountain glows.
pyre.healMsg: A grotto where the lava has cooled to glass. The air is almost bearable. (Checkpoint)
pyre.shrineMsg: You put your hand in the shrine's flame and it doesn't burn. Your shots catch fire, and the mountain stirs.

id.grammar: Three rivers of magma run the height of the mountain and cut it into four banks of basalt. You can cross each river at one permanent basalt causeway, which is never in the same row as the last one, so the route zigzags up and down each bank. Other crossings are crusts of cooling rock that only hold between surges. The summit, the guardian and the antechamber lie past the last river.
id.start: A basalt shelf on the first bank, right on the edge of a magma river: a ring of embers for a portal, the stub of a broken bridge, and a dead pilgrim's pack.
id.landmark: The summit glow. The whole eastern sky burns brighter the closer you get to the pyre, and the rivers themselves show you which way is east.
id.feature: The magma surge. Every fifteen seconds the rivers rise: crust crossings melt back into lava, the burning edge of every bank widens, and when the surge drops the fresh obsidian glows and is brittle for a moment.
id.ante: The Summit Stair: rebirth shells line a stair of black glass up to the pyre where Ignis waits to die again.
traps: The rivers rise on a cycle. Crust crossings melt and the banks burn. The HUD and the glow warn you first.
Vents in the floor erupt in a ring of embers.
Nozzles in the basalt walls breathe fire across the room.
On the ash slopes burning ash falls where its shadow shows.
Some crust crossings crack under you a moment after you step on them.
The edge of the river is liquid fire. Wading in it burns fast.
secrets: A seal of thick obsidian that no shot can break. Right after a surge it glows red and turns brittle for two seconds.
Three cold bowls in a phoenix roost. A phoenixling's rebirth ember lights a bowl it dies next to, and when all three burn the hoard rises.
Phoenixlings come back unless you walk over their embers. Rebirths you prevent are rebirths you don't fight.
A pilgrim who came for the phoenix's ashes, and what he wrote.

lore: The pilgrims climbed with offerings of wood. The bones on the path are the pilgrims.
'Every hundred years it dies. Every hundred years, it comes back angrier.'
An eggshell the size of a cart, still warm.
Someone tried to put the fire out. Their bucket is fused to the rock.
mutations: Sunbirds are common, and so is treasure

zealot.name: Zealot
zealot.how: Rushes you with a burning brand, weaving through the pews, and lunges the last few steps.

flagellant.name: Penitent
flagellant.how: Kneels among the pews as if praying until you come close. Then it rises and flails a ring of blood around itself.

inquisitor.name: Inquisitor
inquisitor.how: Paces the aisles sweeping his lantern. If its light falls on you he names you a heretic: everyone in the room comes for you and you take more damage for a while.

acolyte.name: Ashen Acolyte
acolyte.how: Chants with the requiem. It mends the wounded and throws embers exactly on the beat.

gargoyle.name: Gargoyle
gargoyle.how: Stone until you pass beneath it. Then it wakes on its ledge and spits shards of stained glass. Its skin turns half of every hit.

bat.name: Belfry Bat
bat.how: Pours out of the bell tower in a cloud and flutters at you from all sides.

templar.name: Burned Templar
templar.how: Hides behind a tall shield and guards the others: anything standing near him can't be hurt. Kill him first, or draw them apart.

cherub.name: Gilded Cherub
cherub.how: Rare: a gold cherub from the high altar. It flees, and drops treasure when caught.

archdeacon.name: The Archdeacon
archdeacon.how: Preaches from his burning pulpit. He throws censer-fire that burns where it lands, a ring of embers on every second beat of the requiem, and at half health calls his zealots.
archdeacon.callMsg: The Archdeacon cries out. 'Zealots! To the pulpit!'

cathedral.arrive: The great doors are charred through. Inside, the nave is black with soot, the red carpet still runs toward the altar, and somewhere an organ is playing a requiem.
cathedral.healMsg: One chapel the fire never touched. The candles here are still white. (Checkpoint)
cathedral.shrineMsg: You light the last candle from the shrine. Your shots burn with it, and every eye in the cathedral turns toward you.

id.grammar: Cruciform. A long nave of bays runs west to east along the red carpet, flanked by a north and a south aisle behind the arcades. Fallen roof beams have closed some of the arches between bays, so you detour through an aisle. Side chapels branch off both aisles. The crossing under the fallen spire opens into the transepts, the belfry above and the crypt below; the choir, sometimes reached only round the ambulatory from a transept, leads to the high altar.
id.start: The charred west doors: a narthex with a cracked font full of ash, burned pews, and the start of the red carpet.
id.landmark: The crossing under the fallen spire: a hole in the roof lets the light down onto the burning bell, and the carpet always leads to it and then on to the altar.
id.feature: Fire that still spreads. Hanging censers fall when they're shot and set pews and wood alight, and the fire runs on through anything wooden. The requiem keeps the beat: the choir attacks on it.
id.ante: The Choir Screen: a gilded screen before the high altar, where the Ashen Cardinal finishes his mass.
traps: Embers fall from the burned roof where their shadows show.
Grates in the floor vent burning incense in rows.
On the Censer Walk, censers on long chains sweep across the aisle.
Shoot a censer and the pews around it go up, burning whoever is kneeling there.
If its light finds you, you are branded a heretic.
The transept floor gives way into the crypt beneath.
secrets: A charred wooden panel no shot can break. A censer hangs beside it; drop the censer and the fire burns the panel away.
A side chapel with five candle stands and a hymn board. Light the stands the board shows by brushing past them.
The last confession of the bell-ringer.
The bones under the cathedral, and the dead who guard them.

lore: A confession, scorched at the edges: 'I lit the first candle. I'm sorry. I'm sorry.'
The stained glass is gone. The light that comes through the frames is still red.
'He blessed the fire. Then the fire blessed him back.'
Every pew has a name burned into it, and a date. They're all the same date.
mutations: Thick smoke cuts your sight short
Bishops fill every hall with followers
Gilded Saints are common, and so is treasure

raider.name: Dune Raider
raider.how: Comes at you head on with a curved scimitar and closes the last gap in a sudden lunge.

slinger.name: Slinger
slinger.how: Hangs back on the dunes and whirls stones at you two at a time.

jackal.name: Desert Jackal
jackal.how: Hunts in packs of three or four, weaving in from different sides.

scorpion.name: Giant Scorpion
scorpion.how: Its shell turns aside part of every hit. It lobs its sting at you; the venom stops you healing.

sandworm.name: Sandworm
sandworm.how: Swims under the sand where you can't hit it. It breaches beside you in a ring of grit, then dives again.

mirage.name: Mirage
mirage.how: A raider made of heat haze that wavers toward you. From further than a few steps away your shots pass straight through it; get close and it is real enough to bleed.

obelisk.name: Sun Obelisk
obelisk.how: A stone that wakes in the sun and turns a slow wheel of light around itself.

scarab.name: Golden Scarab
scarab.how: Rare: a scarab of solid gold. It scuttles away, and drops treasure when caught.

duneking.name: The Dune King
duneking.how: Lord of the raiders. He charges with twin blades, fans steel at you, and at half health whistles up his jackal packs.
duneking.callMsg: The Dune King whistles. Jackals come pouring over the dunes.

oasis.arrive: Sand pours through a gate that is half under the dunes. The ground hums. Off to the east, over the ruins, there is a shimmer of green, and water.
oasis.healMsg: Cool water, deep under the sand. You drink, and the heat lets go of you. (Checkpoint)
oasis.shrineMsg: You touch the spring's shrine and turquoise light runs up your arms into your shots. Under the sand, something big turns toward you.

id.grammar: A buried city. Sandstone ruins stand in a loose grid half under the sand, and the oasis lies in the middle. Between ruins run either broad, winding sand passages under the open sun or narrow buried tunnels in the shade. Dune ridges across the sand passages shift between two patterns, so which passages are open keeps changing, though some way through is always open.
id.start: A half-buried city gate. Sand spills in through it, there is a caravan's broken pot, and on the far wall shimmers a pool that isn't there.
id.landmark: The oasis in the middle of the city: palms and a turquoise pool that never dries, seen from the ruins all around it.
id.feature: Sun and sand. Under the open sun you don't recover health, only in the shade of the ruins and tunnels. Drifts slow you, and every eighteen seconds the dunes shift and the open passages change.
id.ante: The Dry Pool: the basin of a second oasis long since drunk dry, where Sarrukh circles beneath the sand.
traps: Ridges of sand rise across the passages and others fall. Sand streams off a ridge just before it moves.
Quicksand halls pull you down in rows; you can see it churn first.
Old darts fly from holes in the sandstone walls.
Ruined ceilings drop stone where the dust falls first.
In the open sun you don't recover health.
They move under the sand and breach next to you.
secrets: Some dune walls shimmer like the false pool at the gate. Walk into one: it was never there.
A swirl of sinking sand beside an obelisk tip. Stand still on it and the sand takes you down into a chamber of the buried city.
A caravan's strongbox lies under one of the shifting ridges. It can only be reached while that ridge is down.
The last caravan to look for the oasis, and its driver's log.

lore: A caravan, buried to the axles. The camels' bells still ring when the wind blows.
'The oasis was here first. Then something drank it.'
A water ration chart. The last entry is 'none'.
The sand here is warm even at night, and it's moving.
mutations: Blowing sand cuts your vision short
Golden Scarabs are common, and so is treasure

bailiff.name: Bailiff
bailiff.how: Marches straight at you and brings his mace down in a ring of cogs exactly on the tick.

clerk.name: Court Clerk
clerk.how: Hides behind the benches and flicks writs at you, one on every tick.

prosecutor.name: Prosecutor
prosecutor.how: Points at you for a long moment, then fires a single clock hand very fast.

windup.name: Wind-up Soldier
windup.how: Clockwork: it stands frozen between ticks, then lurches a stride toward you on every tick and stamps where it lands.

gearorb.name: Gear Orb
gearorb.how: Circles you at a distance, spinning cogs out of its rim in a spiral.

cuckoo.name: Cuckoo
cuckoo.how: Lives in a wall clock. It stays shut, and can't be hurt, until the hour strikes; then it pops out and sprays springs in every direction.

juggernaut.name: Clockwork Juggernaut
juggernaut.how: Iron plate turns a third of every hit. Every few ticks it builds up steam and rams in a straight line.

cog.name: Loose Cog
cog.how: A runaway cog that hops at you in little bounces.

watch.name: Golden Pocket Watch
watch.how: Rare: a gold pocket watch running on tiny legs. It flees, and drops treasure when caught.

chancellor.name: The Chancellor
chancellor.how: Presides from the bench. He fires rings of clock hands on every second tick, a string of writs at you, and at half health winds up his soldiers.
chancellor.callMsg: 'Order!' The Chancellor turns a key, and wind-up soldiers march out.

clocktower.arrive: You hear it before you see it: a vast ticking, under the floor and in the walls. The court is in session, and every door here turns with the clock.
clocktower.healMsg: In this room every clock has stopped. Nothing ticks. You sit for a while and it doesn't count. (Checkpoint)
clocktower.shrineMsg: You set the shrine's little clock going. Your shots keep perfect time, and the whole court turns to look at you.

id.grammar: Mechanical junctions. Round gear hubs sit at the crossings of a grid of passages, with courtrooms between them. Every hub is ringed by a turning brass wall with two gaps in it, and the ring turns an eighth of the way round every three ticks, so the way through a hub depends on when you get there. The Great Clock's own hub stands in the middle.
id.start: The Clock Gate: a brass-trimmed vestibule with a standing clock, scattered writs, and the ticking under the floor.
id.landmark: The Great Clock at the heart of the court. Its hour hand is the HUD clock, and every ring in the building turns in time with it.
id.feature: The tick. Everything keeps time: rings turn every three ticks, gear teeth rise on the tick, the clerks and bailiffs attack on it, and wind-up soldiers only move on it.
id.ante: The Belfry Stair: the clock's own bell hangs at the top of the stair, and the Brass Magistrate holds court beneath it.
traps: Every hub's brass ring turns on a schedule, and it pushes you out of the way if you stand in it.
Teeth come up through the floor on the tick, in rows.
In the pendulum gallery huge blades swing across the hall, each on its own beat.
Wall clocks hold cuckoos that burst out on the hour with a spray of springs.
Wind-up soldiers jump and stamp on the tick. Don't be where they land.
secrets: A clockface painted on a wall. At twelve o'clock exactly it swings open for two ticks, then shuts again.
Three plates marked I, II and III. Step on them in order on three ticks in a row.
The court's own records, and what they say about how long the session has lasted.

lore: A court record. Charge: 'being late.' Sentence: 'forever.'
'Move on the tick. Stand on the tock. Never run.'
Every clock in the tower shows a different time. All of them are wrong in the same way.
A pocketwatch, stopped at the moment its owner was sentenced.
mutations: Magistrates call more help in every hall
Golden Pocketwatches are common, and so is treasure

reflection.name: Your Reflection
reflection.how: Steps out of the glass and moves as your mirror image across the middle of the room, shooting back at you whenever you can see each other.

archer.name: Glass Archer
archer.how: Keeps its distance. Its silvered arrows skip off the walls once before they stop.

prismer.name: Prism
prismer.how: Hangs in the air turning a slow wheel of coloured light.

flicker.name: Flicker
flicker.how: Only half there. It blinks from place to place around you and leaves an afterimage wherever it was.

curator.name: The Curator
curator.how: Stays back and frames new shardlings out of broken glass, three at a time.

golem.name: Glass Golem
golem.how: Every shot that hits it glances straight back at you, except for a moment after it slams the floor.

shardling.name: Shardling
shardling.how: A splinter of mirror that hops at you; three of them come out of every frame.

haunted.name: Haunted Mirror
haunted.how: A standing mirror with someone else's face in it. It lets a reflection out every few seconds until it's broken.

hand.name: Silver Hand Mirror
hand.how: Rare: a hand mirror that scuttles on its handle. It flees, and drops treasure when caught.

doppel.name: The Doppelganger
doppel.how: Your perfect copy, cracked down the middle. It circles you like a reflection in a turning mirror and fires a shot back for every volley you fire; at half health it splits into its reflections.
doppel.callMsg: The Doppelganger cracks, and its reflections step out of it.

mirrors.arrive: You step out of a mirror into a ballroom of mirrors. A hundred of you look back. One of them is a moment late.
mirrors.healMsg: There are no mirrors in this room, and you have no reflection here. It's a relief. (Checkpoint)
mirrors.shrineMsg: In the shrine's glass you see your true face for once. Your shots shine with it, and every reflection in the hall turns to look.

id.grammar: Long galleries stacked in four floors across the mansion, each with a wall of mirror down one side. Some galleries are joined by plain doors and stairs; many are joined only by looking-glasses, mirrors you step into and come out of somewhere else entirely, often nowhere near where you would expect. Some passages simply end in a mirror.
id.start: The Front Glass: you come out of a looking-glass into a gallery whose whole north wall is mirror, and your reflection walks alongside you.
id.landmark: The mirror walls themselves. Each gallery reflects the wall opposite it, and the reflection always tells the truth about it.
id.feature: Reflection. Shots, yours and theirs, glance off mirror walls. Looking-glasses carry you between galleries. Reflections walk as your mirror image.
id.ante: The Last Mirror: a gallery that ends in one great mirror, and Vitrea in every pane of it.
traps: Every shot that hits a mirror pane bounces off it, yours included.
Spines of glass come up through the polished floor in rows.
Beams of light sweep the corridor from a turning lens.
A mirror you step into can leave you on another floor of the mansion.
Standing mirrors let reflections out until you break them.
secrets: A mirror wall shows a doorway in the wall opposite it where there seems to be only wall. The reflection is right: walk into that wall.
A lamp, a crystal and turning mirrors. Step on a mirror's plate to turn it, and steer the beam onto the crystal.
Notes from the glassblower who made the first mirror here.

lore: Your reflection here is a second late. In the next room, it's a second early.
'Never be the one who blinks first.'
A glassblower's notes: 'She asked for a mirror that shows what you could be.'
One of the frames is empty. Its label has your name on it.
mutations: Gilt Frames are common, and so is treasure

monk.name: Fallen Monk
monk.how: Sits in meditation until you come near, then flows at you and strikes with an open palm that knocks you back.

beadthrower.name: Bead Novice
beadthrower.how: Whirls a string of prayer beads and lets it fly in a curving chain.

slinger.name: Temple Slinger
slinger.how: Crouches out of reach and lobs stones over walls and pillars at where you're standing.

kiteman.name: Kite Monk
kiteman.how: Glides on a paper kite out over the sky and swoops back in to drop stones on you.

wheelspirit.name: Prayer Wheel
